bundles.name: Identity and Legal Frame
bundles.description: What this agreement is, how it is uniquely denoted, what kind of transaction it governs and which law and forum apply to it.
bundles.rationale: Before any term can be read or any obligation operated, an agent must fix the record's identity boundary and the legal regime that determines validity, interpretation, performance and remedies; the HCCH Principles make the chosen law govern exactly those matters.

layers.name: Agreement Identity and Classification
layers.description: Denotation of the agreement instance and the coded classification that selects the applicable regime and term expectations.

findings.name: Agreement Record Identity and Instance Boundary
findings.description: How one agreement is distinguished from another, which identifier is authoritative, and where a framework agreement ends and a call-off begins.

findings.name: Subject-Matter Classification and Applicable Regime
findings.description: Coded classification of what the agreement does, and the declared applicability or exclusion of regimes such as the CISG.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is coded reference data asserted on the agreement record and resolved against external code lists; it produces no separate document. The evidence for a regime exclusion is the clause artifact already held by the clause-addressability finding, so duplicating an artifact here would fragment the executed text.

layers.name: Applicable Law and Dispute Forum
layers.description: The chosen governing law, the mandatory rules it cannot displace, and the forum agreed for disputes together with the form evidence that forum requires.

findings.name: Governing Law and Mandatory Rules
findings.description: Which law the parties chose, whether expressly or tacitly, the severability of that choice, and the overriding rules that apply regardless.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The governing-law declaration is an attribute of the agreement plus a pointer into the executed clause tree; the clause text itself is the artifact of the clause-addressability finding. Minting a separate artifact would create a second, divergent copy of a normative provision.

findings.name: Dispute Forum, Escalation and Written-Form Evidence
findings.description: The agreed forum, escalation ladder and seat, plus the writing evidence an arbitration agreement needs to be enforceable across borders.

bundles.name: Parties, Identity and Authority
bundles.description: Who is bound, in what role, on whose behalf, and with what verified power to bind.
bundles.rationale: A contract binds legal persons through positions filled by representatives; UNIDROIT treats authority of agents as a distinct chapter and the LEI provides a governed identifier, so party position, party identity and signing authority are separable decision surfaces.

layers.name: Party Positions and Legal Identification
layers.description: The roles the agreement creates and the verified real-world entities that occupy them.

findings.name: Party Position and Contractual Role
findings.description: The abstract positions the agreement creates, their roles, and how liability is shared where several parties occupy one side.
findings.inline_only_rationale: A party position is a structural slot in the agreement record, not a document. Its evidence is the executed text and the identity verification record held by the neighbouring finding; creating an artifact for a slot would assert a document that does not exist.

findings.name: Legal Identification and Place of Business
findings.description: The governed identifier for each party, the verification evidence behind it, and the place of business that drives regime applicability.

layers.name: Authority and Representation
layers.description: The power of the individuals and intermediaries who bind the parties, and the positions of third parties who are affected without signing.

findings.name: Signing Authority and Capacity
findings.description: Who executed the agreement for each party, on what basis they were empowered, and what limits bounded that power.

findings.name: Agents, Guarantors and Third-Party Beneficiaries
findings.description: Positions held by parties who act for, secure or benefit from the agreement without being principal obligors.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Third-party positions are structural relations derived from the executed clauses; where a guarantee or agency is itself a separate agreement, it is a distinct instance of this model rather than an artifact of this finding, which avoids double-owning another contract's text.

bundles.name: Formation, Execution and Effectiveness
bundles.description: How the agreement came into existence, how consent was expressed and evidenced, and when it began to bite.
bundles.rationale: The CISG devotes a whole Part to formation by offer and acceptance, the UN electronic communications convention governs dispatch and receipt of the messages that carry consent, and eIDAS and the UNCITRAL Model Law govern the evidentiary weight of the resulting signature.

layers.name: Consent and Conclusion
layers.description: The offer, acceptance or conduct that concluded the agreement, and whose standard terms became part of it.

findings.name: Offer, Acceptance and Incorporated Standard Terms
findings.description: The communications and conduct that concluded the contract, when and where they took effect, and which standard terms were incorporated when both sides sent their own.

layers.name: Execution and Effectiveness
layers.description: The signature or seal evidence attached to the agreed text, and the conditions that had to be met before it took effect.

findings.name: Execution, Signature Type and Form Requirement
findings.description: How the agreement was signed or sealed, the assurance level and validation evidence of that signature, and any form requirement it had to satisfy.

findings.name: Conditions Precedent, Effectiveness and Validity Defects
findings.description: The gap between execution and effect: conditions to be satisfied, approvals to be obtained, and defects that can unwind consent.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Effectiveness is a computed state over conditions, clauses and events already held elsewhere; the documents that satisfy a condition (a regulatory approval, a guarantee) are artifacts owned by their own models or by the notice finding. Creating an artifact here would duplicate them.

bundles.name: Agreed Text and Commercial Terms
bundles.description: The structure of the agreed text, the documents that make it up, and the substantive commercial and protective terms it contains.
bundles.rationale: Operating a contract requires addressing individual provisions stably across amendments, knowing which documents govern when they conflict, and reading the price, delivery and protective terms as structured values rather than prose.

layers.name: Document Structure and Precedence
layers.description: How provisions are addressed, which documents constitute the contract, how conflicts between them resolve, and which language governs.

findings.name: Clause Addressability and Structure
findings.description: Stable identification of individual provisions across versions, their classification and their machine-readable form.

findings.name: Constituent Documents, Precedence and Authentic Language
findings.description: Which documents together form the contract, how conflicts between them are ranked, and which language version controls.

findings.name: Interpretation, usages and subsequent conduct
findings.description: CISG Article 8 interprets statements and conduct first by a party's intent where the other party knew or could not have been unaware of it, otherwise by a reasonable person of the same kind in the same circumstances, having regard to negotiations, practices, usages and subsequent conduct. Article 9 binds parties to agreed usages and established practices and, unless otherwise agreed, to international trade usages they knew or ought to have known. Article 7 requires interpretation of the Convention itself with regard to international character, uniformity and good faith. UNIDROIT Chapter 4 (as part of PICC 2016) supplies complementary interpretation and gap-filling. These materials are evidence for meaning, not a second contract.

layers.name: Commercial and Protective Terms
layers.description: Price and payment, delivery and risk, and the warranty, liability, confidentiality and compliance terms that allocate exposure.

findings.name: Price, Consideration and Payment Terms
findings.description: How the price is fixed or determined, in what currency, when payment falls due and what follows late payment.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Payment terms are structured values derived from clauses; the payment schedule itself is held by the milestone finding and the resulting invoices belong to a settlement model. Asserting a separate artifact here would either duplicate the clause text or claim ownership of financial documents outside this model's boundary.

findings.name: Delivery Terms, Risk Transfer and Conformity
findings.description: The trade term governing delivery and cost allocation, the point at which risk passes, and the conformity and inspection regime.

findings.name: Warranty, Liability, Confidentiality and Compliance Terms
findings.description: Terms that allocate risk and constrain conduct: warranties, liability caps and exclusions, indemnities, confidentiality, intellectual property, data protection and fairness controls.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are structured readings of clauses already carried by the clause tree artifact. Holding them as separate artifacts would create a normatively significant second copy of contract wording whose divergence from the executed text could not be detected.

bundles.name: Obligations, Performance and Variance
bundles.description: What the agreement requires, when it falls due, what actually happened, and how the parties change or end it.
bundles.rationale: The uniform sales regime and the UNIDROIT Principles both organise the operative life of a contract around obligations, performance, non-performance, excuse and remedy; LegalRuleML supplies the machine-readable deontic form of those duties.

layers.name: Obligations and Schedule
layers.description: The duties the agreement creates and the temporal conditions that make them performable or overdue.

findings.name: Obligation as Deontic Specification
findings.description: Each duty expressed with its deontic type, bearer, auxiliary party, source clause and the violation and reparation that follow non-compliance.

findings.name: Milestones, Due Conditions and Cure Periods
findings.description: The calendar and event conditions that make a duty performable or overdue, together with grace and cure periods.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Milestones are computed projections over obligations, dates and events. Any published schedule is a projection artifact governed by the interoperability finding; a standalone schedule artifact here would risk becoming an authoritative timetable that diverges from the clauses that generate it.

layers.name: Performance and Non-Performance
layers.description: What was rendered and accepted, and what happens when performance fails, is excused or triggers a remedy.

findings.name: Performance Record, Measurement and Acceptance
findings.description: Evidence that a duty was performed, the measured result against agreed criteria, and the counterparty's acceptance or rejection.

findings.name: Non-Performance, Excuse and Remedy
findings.description: Declared failure to perform, its severity, any excuse such as impediment or hardship, and the remedy elected or agreed.

findings.name: Breach, additional time, cure, suspension and anticipatory breach
findings.description: CISG Article 25 defines fundamental breach as detriment that substantially deprives the other party of what it is entitled to expect, unless the result was not foreseeable. Articles 47 and 63 allow a Nachfrist additional period of reasonable length; during it the fixing party may not resort to inconsistent remedies but keeps damages for delay. Articles 71–72 allow suspension for apparent future non-performance of a substantial part, with immediate notice and a duty to continue if adequate assurance is provided, and avoidance for clear future fundamental breach. Article 73 deals with instalments. LegalRuleML Violation, Suborder, Penalty and Reparation model the deontic consequence of breach. A breach declaration is a party event, not a court judgment; adjudication is a sibling process.

layers.name: Change, Communication and Closure
layers.description: Amendment of the terms, transfer of positions, the formal notices that operate the contract, and the way it ends.

findings.name: Amendment and Variation
findings.description: Agreed changes to the terms, the formality they require, the clauses they touch and the version they produce.

findings.name: Assignment, Novation and Change of Control
findings.description: Transfer of rights or of a whole position to a successor, the consent it requires, and its effect on the record's continuity.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Where the transfer is documented, that document is an executed amendment or a separate agreement instance and is already covered by those findings. Recording a duplicate artifact here would create two independent chains of title over the same position.

findings.name: Notices and Formal Communication
findings.description: The formal messages that operate the contract, the channels and addresses they must use, and the rules that deem them received.

findings.name: Termination, Expiry and Survival
findings.description: How the agreement ends, on what ground, which provisions survive and what wind-down obligations remain.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Termination is effected by a notice, an expiry of term, or an amendment-like release, all of which are already held as artifacts by the notice and amendment findings. The end state itself is a derived status over those events plus the clause tree.

bundles.name: Record Governance, Evidence and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the jointly owned record stays trustworthy, who may see what, how long it is kept, and how it is exchanged without leaking terms.
bundles.rationale: Records management standards make authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability the defining properties of a record and require metadata and disposition control; provenance vocabulary and interchange standards make those properties expressible across systems.

layers.name: Provenance and Integrity
layers.description: Attribution of every assertion in the record and cryptographic fixity of the executed text.

findings.name: Provenance, Attribution and Text Integrity
findings.description: Who or what generated each assertion, from which source it was derived, when, and what digest and signature evidence fixes the executed text against later alteration.

layers.name: Access, Retention and Exchange
layers.description: Confidentiality of the joint record, its disposition over time, and the projections through which it interoperates.

findings.name: Access, Disclosure and Redaction
findings.description: Who may read which part of the joint record, under what grant and purpose, and how compelled disclosure is handled.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Access grants are governed records owned by the access-grant model and referenced here; the evidence of each access is an entry in the provenance and audit log artifact. A separate artifact would fork authority over grants away from their owning model.

findings.name: Retention, Limitation Periods and Disposition
findings.description: How long the record must be kept, what suspends deletion, and how authorised disposition is carried out and evidenced.

findings.name: External Alignment and Projections
findings.description: Declared alignments to external vocabularies and the reduced views published to non-parties, with what each view omits.

model.name: Obligation / Commitment
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral structure for a directed deontic commitment: which party owes which action or forbearance, to whom, under which conditions, by when, to what standard, how it is discharged, and what follows if it is not.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-029 models a single obligation/commitment instance as a mixin that can be attached to any host record that creates or carries duties (contract clause, statute or regulation article, licence, court or administrative order, service commitment, internal policy, unilateral promise). It covers the deontic core (bearer, counterparty, modality, action), the conditional structure that detaches the duty, the temporal structure (due time, recurrence, grace, limitation), the lifecycle state model, fulfilment and its evidence, non-performance with excuse and remedy, the authority and provenance that make the duty defensible, and transfer, plurality and standards alignment. It deliberately does not model the instrument, the parties, the executed work or the accounting recognition; those are referenced from sibling models.
in_scope: Deontic modality of a single duty (obligation, prohibition, correlative right) and whether it is violable rather than definitional
Bearer/obligor, obligee, beneficiary, auxiliary and enforcing party roles for one commitment
Obligated action or forbearance, its controlled action term, refinements and subject matter or target
Antecedent and resolutive conditions, detachment, and the constraint expressions that gate the duty
Due instant or performance window, recurrence, grace, notice, survival and limitation periods
Lifecycle states and transitions with separate event time and observation/ingestion time
Fulfilment criteria, acceptance, discharge mode, partial performance and measure of progress
Fulfilment evidence, its issuer, integrity and status
Non-performance determination, excuse grounds, cure periods, remedy and penalty obligations
Legal or policy basis, issuing authority, jurisdiction and governing law of the duty
Record ownership, stewardship, provenance and audit trail of the obligation record
Assignment of the correlative right, transfer or novation of the duty, plurality of obligors/obligees and apportionment
Confidentiality classification, personal-data flags, retention and legal hold on obligation records
Crosswalk to ODRL Duty, LegalRuleML Obligation, FIBO contractual commitment, IFRS 15 performance obligation and compliance-obligation registers
out_of_scope: The agreement or contract instrument itself, its formation, offer/acceptance, consideration and clause text
Legal-entity identity, registration, legal capacity and party master data
Generic policy containers and rule engines, including access-control decision points and their evaluation infrastructure
Execution of work: tasks, work orders, scheduling, resourcing and dispatch
Payment initiation, clearing and settlement mechanics and ledger postings
Accounting recognition and measurement of liabilities, provisions and revenue amounts
Dispute, arbitration and litigation case management
Risk registers, control design and control-effectiveness testing
Consent capture and consent lifecycle as a lawful basis
Calendar, holiday and business-day-convention definitions themselves
Definitional or structural necessities that cannot be violated
Signature, sealing and e-signature ceremony records

boundary_notes.distinction: An agreement is a negotiated understanding reflecting offer and acceptance of commitments; a commitment is a promise by one party to act or refrain. One agreement carries many obligations, and an obligation can exist with no agreement at all (statute, court order, unilateral commitment, commitment at large). This model references the instrument and never restates its terms.

ODRL places Duties inside a Policy, either as a policy-level obligation or as a pre-condition duty on a Permission. This mixin sits at the Rule/Duty level, not the container level; the policy grouping, conflict strategy and inheritance belong to the policy model.

A right is the reciprocal aspect of a commitment and is borne by a different party; LegalRuleML models a Right as a permission to a bearer that implies obligations on auxiliary parties. The correlative right is referenced, not duplicated, so that assignment of the right and transfer of the duty stay separable.

A prohibition is violated by performing the act, an obligation by failing to perform it. The modality and violation polarity are recorded here, but negative-duty enforcement semantics (remedy on infringement) differ from consequence semantics on unfulfilled duties and must not be collapsed.

A task is an execution artefact. Several tasks may contribute to discharging one obligation, and tasks exist with no obligation behind them. Progress measurement is carried here only as a discharge measure, not as work scheduling.

IFRS 15 performance obligations are only promises to transfer distinct goods or services to a customer; obligations outside that definition fall to other standards. Recognition, measurement and presentation of the financial effect are out of scope and belong to a financial-reporting model.

ODRL defines Constraint as leftOperand/operator/rightOperand and LogicalConstraint as and/or/xone/andSequence. This model references those expression structures and their operand vocabularies rather than redefining operators.

A compliance management system maintains a register of obligations the organisation must or voluntarily chooses to meet. That register is a collection-level and programme-level concern; this model describes one obligation entry and does not carry control design or assurance results.

SBVR separates alethic necessities, which cannot be violated even in principle, from deontic obligations, which may be violated although they ought not to be. Structural necessities must not be represented as obligations in this model.

PROV-O supplies the entity/activity/agent vocabulary for how the obligation record came to be. This model aligns to it and carries the minimum provenance fields inline; the full provenance graph belongs to the provenance model.

functions.name: Register obligation
functions.description: Create an obligation record from a source instrument clause, statutory article, order or voluntary commitment, populating the deontic core and the source citation.
inputs: Source instrument reference and clause locator
Obligor and, where directed, obligee references
outputs: Obligation register entry with an assigned identifier
Provenance entry for the creating activity
preconditions: The source instrument version is resolvable and its clause locator is valid
The action term resolves in a declared action vocabulary
The obligor reference resolves in the party model
effects: A new obligation identity exists in the register
The obligation enters the proposed or active state with both event and ingestion timestamps recorded

functions.name: Classify obligation
functions.description: Assign modality, violability, achievement or maintenance kind, effort standard, primary or secondary status and compliance category, with the criteria applied.
preconditions: The classification scheme version is published and effective
The obligated action is stated
effects: Downstream evaluation and measurement rules are selected by the assigned classes
Alethic statements are rejected from the obligation register

functions.name: Evaluate antecedent and detach
functions.description: Evaluate the obligation's antecedent and constraint set against observed operand values and, when satisfied, detach the obligation so that it becomes due.
inputs: Observed operand values with their observation times
preconditions: All left operands resolve in a recognised profile
The evaluator recognises every declared profile identifier
effects: The obligation transitions to detached or remains conditional
A durable, replayable evaluation record is appended

functions.name: Compute due schedule
functions.description: Derive due instants and performance windows from the due basis, recurrence rule, time zone, business-day convention and any trigger events.
inputs: Time zone, calendar and business-day convention
outputs: Due date schedule with nominal and adjusted instants
preconditions: The calendar and business-day convention references resolve
Every input instant carries an explicit offset or Z
effects: Occurrences become individually addressable and monitorable
Deadline computation becomes reproducible from recorded inputs

functions.name: Evaluate fulfilment
functions.description: Determine whether the obligation is fulfilled by testing constraint satisfaction and exercise of the refined action, accounting for quantity, acceptance and any consequence duties.
preconditions: Evidence supporting exercise of the action is present and unrevoked
Acceptance has been given or is not required
effects: The obligation transitions toward fulfilled, partly fulfilled or unchanged
Outstanding balances are recomputed

functions.name: Record fulfilment evidence
functions.description: Attach evidence of performance to an obligation or occurrence with its issuer, validity interval, integrity proof and status, and bind it to the quantity it discharges.
preconditions: The issuer is recognised as competent for this evidence type
The integrity proof verifies against the evidence
effects: Discharge becomes independently re-verifiable
Later revocation of the evidence can reopen the determination

functions.name: Declare non-performance
functions.description: Determine and formally declare non-performance after the due time and grace period, classify it, assess materiality and serve any required notice.
inputs: Evidence of failure, defect or lateness
outputs: Breach or default notice with proof of service
preconditions: The grace period has expired without discharge
No accepted excuse ground is in force
The declaring party is authorised
effects: Consequence and remedy obligations become eligible for creation
The dispute status field becomes available for contestation

functions.name: Apply remedy or penalty
functions.description: Create the consequence, remedy or penalty obligations triggered by non-fulfilment or infringement, compute amounts against the formula and cap, and link them to the breached obligation.
inputs: Penalty formula, cap and accrual basis
outputs: Links from the breached obligation to its consequences
preconditions: Breach has been declared and any cure period has expired
The consequence definition does not itself carry a further consequence in the exchange projection
effects: Secondary obligations enter the register with their own lifecycles
The original obligation remains open until both it and its consequences are fulfilled

functions.name: Transfer obligation or assign right
functions.description: Record assignment of the correlative right, transfer of the duty, delegation of performance or novation, applying the identity continuity rule and any release of the original obligor.
preconditions: The right or duty is transferable under the governing instrument
Any required consent or notice has been obtained and evidenced
effects: Party roles change from the effective instant
Identity is preserved for delegation and replaced for release-and-substitute novation

functions.name: Transition obligation state
functions.description: Apply a permitted state transition, recording the prior and new state, the basis, the acting agent, the event time and the observation time.
inputs: Current state and proposed target state
outputs: Updated current state and terminal flag
preconditions: The transition is permitted by the declared transition matrix
The acting agent holds the required authority for asserted transitions
effects: The obligation history remains reconstructible at any past instant
Terminal states block further transitions except authorised reopening

functions.name: Report obligation register
functions.description: Produce a filtered, access-controlled view of obligations by owner, state, due window, jurisdiction or source, for monitoring, management review and assurance.
preconditions: The requester holds read access at the requested scope
Confidentiality classifications are resolved for every selected row
effects: Register currency and coverage become measurable
Every disclosure is auditable

functions.name: Apply retention and close
functions.description: Evaluate the retention trigger, enforceability window and legal holds, then archive, tombstone or destroy the obligation record and its evidence, certifying the outcome.
preconditions: No legal hold is in force
Retention justification has been reviewed against the limitation determination
effects: Records are removed or reduced to tombstones while referential integrity is preserved
Data-protection storage limitation is demonstrably observed

functions.name: Offer cure or grant additional period
functions.description: Apply UNIDROIT 7.1.4 cure or 7.1.5 additional period, suspending inconsistent remedies until the period expires.
inputs: notice of cure or additional period
preconditions: non-performance has occurred
cure is appropriate and notice is timely
effects: inconsistent remedies suspended until expiry
aggrieved party may still withhold and claim delay damages

composition.target: Host record carrying duties (contract clause, statute or regulation article, licence condition, service commitment, internal policy statement, unilateral pledge)
composition.purpose: WM-XCT-029 is applied to any host record that creates or carries a duty, supplying the deontic core, conditions, due structure, lifecycle and fulfilment semantics without changing the host's own identity or content model.
Resolve the instrument, its version and the clause locator that creates a contractual obligation; the instrument's formation, consideration and clause text stay in that model.
Resolve obligor, obligee, beneficiary, performing, enforcing and monitoring party references, including legal capacity, without duplicating party master data.
Link the correlative right created by the commitment so that assignment of the right and transfer of the duty remain separately governed.
Compose the antecedent, refinement and rule constraints from a shared expression structure of left operand, operator, right operand, unit and logical combination.

composition.target: Obligation / Commitment (WM-XCT-029) as consequence, remedy or penalty obligation
composition.purpose: Secondary obligations created by non-fulfilment or infringement are themselves obligations and recurse onto this model rather than being modelled as flat penalty attributes.
Resolve fulfilment evidence, notices, certificates and their issuers, validity intervals, proofs and revocation status.

Align obligation-record provenance to Entity, Activity and Agent with generation, derivation, attribution, association and delegation, so that derived obligations remain traceable to their source clause.
Provide a machine-evaluable exchange projection for duties, actions, constraints, consequences and remedies, with recorded divergences on asset targeting and consequence nesting.

composition.target: OASIS LegalRuleML 1.0 Obligation, Violation and PenaltyStatement
composition.purpose: Provide a legal-norm exchange projection carrying bearer, auxiliary party, violation, compliance, reparation, authority, jurisdiction and temporal characteristics.
Flag the narrower accounting subset of promises and their satisfaction pattern, without importing recognition or measurement into this model.
Supply the per-entry structure that a compliance obligations register aggregates, covering both externally imposed requirements and voluntary commitments.
Resolve retention triggers, periods, legal holds and destruction treatment for obligation records and their evidence.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension MUST designate one accountable owner package for WM-XCT-029 and record it in the Dimension registry before any obligation record is created; unowned obligation records MUST be rejected at creation.

The owner package MUST publish and version the controlled vocabularies this model depends on — deontic modality, violability class, obligation kind, effort standard, discharge mode, state set and transition matrix, breach type, excuse ground and transfer type — as resolvable terms with effective dates.

The owner package MUST declare which host models may mix in this model and which sibling models are referenced rather than duplicated, and MUST re-declare that list whenever a sibling model changes its scope.

The owner package MUST nominate a legal or compliance reviewer accountable for jurisdiction-bearing fields (governing law, limitation, survival, enforcement authority) and MUST NOT allow those fields to be set by automated extraction without review.
The owner package MUST maintain the alignment crosswalk with pinned versions of every target vocabulary and MUST record divergences rather than silently adapting them.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint obligation identifiers and vocabulary terms in a single stable namespace controlled by the owner package, segmented by concern (obligations, occurrences, states, actions, excuse grounds). Never reuse an external standard's namespace for locally defined terms; where a local term corresponds to an external one, record the correspondence in the crosswalk with an explicit mapping relation. Term IRIs are opaque and permanent: retire terms by deprecation with a replacement pointer, never by reuse or deletion. Occurrence keys are minted under the parent obligation's namespace so that they remain resolvable after the parent is superseded.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-029 (WM-XCT-029, entry kind mixin, nav path NAV.XCT.OBL, domain tag XCT.OBL) is the authoritative registration for this model and MUST carry the owner package and review state.
The registry entry MUST link to the sibling models named in the composition section once their registry identifiers exist, replacing the descriptive target names used here.

The registry entry MUST record the review state boundary-review-required until the boundaries against the agreement, right, policy and compliance-register models have been signed off by the nominated reviewer.

canonicalization_rules: All timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; the originally stated local time, its time zone identifier and its business-day convention are retained alongside the canonical instant and are never discarded.
Code values are canonicalised to their governed term IRIs; display labels are derived, never stored as the authoritative value.
Quantities are canonicalised as an explicit value-plus-unit pair, and monetary amounts as an explicit amount-plus-currency pair; bare numbers are rejected.
Absent and empty are distinguished: an omitted element means not asserted, an explicit null means asserted as not applicable, and an empty collection means asserted as none.
References are canonicalised to resolvable identifiers with the referenced version pinned where the referent is versioned, so that a citation continues to mean what it meant when recorded.
patch_rules: Patches address stable element identifiers, never positional paths, so that reordering a collection never changes the meaning of a stored patch.
State changes are appended as transitions and never applied as in-place overwrites of the current state; the current state is a derived projection of the transition log.

Changes to deontic modality, obligor, obligated action, due basis or governing law create a new version with a supersedes link rather than mutating the existing record, because these fields change what the obligation is.
Every patch carries the acting agent, the reason code, the event time and the ingestion time; a patch missing any of these is rejected.
Corrections to historical facts are recorded as corrective entries that preserve the superseded value, so that what the register said at any past instant remains reconstructible.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element, a new vocabulary term or a new alignment mapping is a minor change.

Adding a required element, narrowing a cardinality, removing an element, or removing or redefining a state, modality or discharge-mode code is a breaking change and requires a major version and a migration note.
Changing the transition matrix to forbid a previously permitted transition is breaking; adding a permitted transition is minor only if no terminal state gains an outbound transition.

Retargeting the crosswalk to a new version of an external vocabulary is minor when the conformance claim is unchanged, and breaking when a previously asserted conformance claim is withdrawn or narrowed.
Consumers MUST tolerate unknown optional elements, and MUST stop processing rather than guess when they encounter an unrecognised profile identifier.

identity_priority: Use the identifier assigned by the authoritative master system for the obligation where such a master exists, for example the obligation identifier issued by a contract-management or regulatory-register system of record.
Otherwise use a governed global identifier or IRI minted in the owner package's obligation namespace, resolvable and permanent.
Otherwise mint a UUID or ULID under the adopting Dimension's control and record the minting agent and instant.
A due date, a clause number, a party name or any combination of descriptive attributes is never an identifier; such combinations may serve only as declared match keys for deduplication.
Occurrence identity is always composite: the standing obligation identifier plus the occurrence key generated by the recorded recurrence rule version.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every timestamp is an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Event time (when the fact took legal effect) and observation or ingestion time (when the system learned of it) are recorded as separate elements and are never collapsed; where a legally relevant local civil time exists, its time zone identifier and business-day convention are stored alongside the canonical instant. The RFC 3339 -00:00 form is used only to mean that the local offset is genuinely unknown and is never written as a synonym for Z.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts — state transition log entries, condition evaluation entries, progress measurements, acceptance certificates, breach notices, remedy determinations, assignment records and audit entries — are numbered within a series scoped to one obligation identifier, using a gapless monotonically increasing integer with no semantic content. The series name encodes the artefact class and the obligation identifier; gaps are treated as evidence of loss and must be investigated, and numbers are never reissued after voiding.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Append-only artefacts (state transition log, condition evaluation log, provenance and change audit trail) carry a per-entry integrity digest chained to the preceding entry, so that removal or alteration of any entry is detectable. Externally issued evidence retains its issuer's proof and status endpoint unaltered; the register stores the verification outcome and instant rather than re-signing the evidence. Any artefact whose integrity check fails is quarantined, flagged on the obligation record and excluded from fulfilment evaluation until resolved.

policies: An obligation record MUST NOT be created without a resolvable source instrument reference and a clause, article or paragraph-level citation; obligations asserted without a stated basis are held as candidates and excluded from the operative register.
Alethic statements MUST NOT be registered as obligations; a statement that cannot in principle be violated belongs to the definitional vocabulary, not to the obligation register.

Conformance to an external standard MUST NOT be claimed without a dated validation report from a named validator; absent that evidence, only alignment may be asserted and the divergences must be listed.

Automated extraction MAY populate an obligation record, but jurisdiction-bearing fields and any transition into breached, waived, released or discharged states MUST be attributable to an authorised human or explicitly delegated agent.

Deleting an obligation record is prohibited while it is within its enforceability window or under legal hold; disposal outside those constraints proceeds through the retention function and produces a destruction or tombstone record.

Fulfilment MUST NOT be asserted on the basis of elapsed time alone; discharge requires the recorded fulfilment test to be satisfied or an explicit discharge mode such as waiver, release, set-off or expiry to be recorded with its instrument.
Fulfilment cannot be asserted without linked evidence unless an authorised waiver exception is recorded.
Access-control, legal and contractual senses of obligation MUST keep distinct deontic-kind-code values and MUST NOT be merged in queries by English label alone.
Original duties remain required after consequence attachment unless an explicit discharge is recorded, matching ODRL consequence semantics.
Logical discharge is preferred to physical delete; physical delete is blocked during legal hold and while statutory retention runs.
Constraint evaluation precedes overdue and violation assertions; force-majeure and interference excuses must be coded rather than inferred from silence.

read: Reading an obligation returns its current state as a projection of the transition log together with the event and ingestion timestamps of the latest transition.

Reads are filtered by confidentiality classification and requester role; suppressed elements are reported as suppressed rather than silently omitted, so that consumers cannot mistake redaction for absence.
Historical reads at a past instant MUST be supported and MUST return what the register asserted at that instant, not the current values.
create: Creation requires identifier assignment under the identity priority, a source citation, a deontic modality, an obligated action and an obligor; records failing any of these are rejected, not stored as partial.
Creation records the generating activity, the attributed agent and both creation and ingestion timestamps.
Creating a recurring obligation also records the recurrence rule version used, so that generated occurrences can be replayed.
update: Content-defining fields (modality, obligor, action, due basis, governing law) are updated only by versioning with a supersedes link; other fields are patched in place with a reason code and dual timestamps.
State is never updated directly; it changes only through the recorded transition function against the declared transition matrix.
Updates to a superseded version are prohibited; corrections apply to the current version and cite the superseded one.
delete: Hard deletion is prohibited for obligations within their enforceability window, under legal hold, or referenced by an open secondary obligation.
End-of-retention disposal reduces the record to a tombstone retaining the identifier, the disposal decision and the destruction certificate reference, so that inbound references do not dangle.
Append-only logs are never deleted individually; they are disposed only as whole series under a recorded retention decision, and the disposal is itself logged.

roles.name: Obligation Model Owner
responsibilities: Own the specification, vocabularies and version history of WM-XCT-029 within the adopting Dimension
Approve breaking changes, migrations and the declared list of host and sibling models
Maintain the registry entry and drive the outstanding boundary review to closure

roles.name: Obligation Registrar / Steward
responsibilities: Create and maintain obligation records, assign identifiers under the identity priority and keep source citations accurate
Run currency reviews at the declared cadence and attest that register entries remain correct
Resolve duplicate and merge decisions against the declared match key

roles.name: Legal and Compliance Reviewer
responsibilities: Review and approve modality, violability, governing law, jurisdiction, limitation and survival determinations
Approve breach declarations, excuse determinations and waiver or release decisions
Record conflicts between jurisdictions or between this model and external vocabularies rather than resolving them silently

roles.name: Performance Monitor
responsibilities: Track due schedules, grace expiry and progress measurements and raise alerts within the declared lead times
Attach fulfilment evidence and record verification outcomes
Escalate impending or actual non-performance along the recorded escalation path

roles.name: Records and Retention Officer
responsibilities: Apply retention triggers, legal holds and disposition to obligation records and their evidence
Issue destruction certificates and maintain tombstone integrity
Reconcile erasure requests against enforceability-window and legal-claim retention justifications

roles.name: Interoperability Custodian
responsibilities: Maintain the alignment crosswalk with pinned target-vocabulary versions and recorded divergences
Run validators against exchange projections and retain dated validation reports
Block conformance claims that lack validation evidence

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access is granted per scope to named roles, and every grant carries a purpose and an expiry; obligation records are readable only by roles with a declared need arising from ownership, monitoring, legal review, assurance or a party's own involvement.
exceptions: The obligor and obligee of an obligation may read the findings and artefacts describing their own duty, its due structure, its fulfilment state and the evidence relied on against them, even where the general classification is more restrictive.
Auditors, supervisory authorities and courts may be granted time-boxed read access across all scopes for a stated proceeding, recorded as an exception with its legal basis, scope and expiry.
Legal hold suspends any access restriction that would prevent preservation, but does not by itself widen read access.

Automated evaluators may read constraint expressions, operand values and state at finding scope without access to free-text clause extracts or personal data, so that evaluation does not require broad disclosure.
Legal hold and regulatory examination may extend read to named investigators without making them stewards.
CommitmentAtLarge public instruments may be read more widely than bilateral duties.
PEP obligation payloads may be visible to runtime enforcement components that are not party to the underlying commercial duty.
audit_requirements: Every read, export and access-exception grant is logged with the requester, role, scope, purpose, decision and RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset.
Every state transition, version supersession and patch is logged with acting agent, reason code, event time and ingestion time in the append-only audit trail.
Access to obligation records containing personal data is separately reportable so that disclosure can be reconstructed for a data-subject or supervisory request.
Audit trails are retained for at least the enforceability window of the obligation they concern and are disposed of only under a recorded retention decision.
Log every create, state transition, evidence attach, consequence attach, waiver and delete with actor, event time, observation time and previous state.
Audit logs retain ObligationId/uid aliases used at the time of the action.
Evaluation results (active, overdue, fulfilled, violated) are attributable to a named evaluator or system.

read_order: AGENTS.md — establish Name, Type, owner package, registry identifier and the four required URLs before touching any record
Specification URL — read the model scope, boundaries, bundle/layer/finding structure and the required elements, so that records are interpreted with the correct semantics
Storage type URL — learn the concrete projection in use (document store, graph, files under version control, or a service) and the canonicalisation and patch rules that apply to it
Interface URL — learn the available operations, their authorisation scopes and the required timestamp and identifier formats
Processes URL — learn the registration, classification, evaluation, breach, remedy, transfer and retention procedures and the roles authorised to run them
Vocabulary namespace and alignment crosswalk — resolve controlled terms and check pinned external vocabulary versions before producing any exchange projection

coverage.claim: The adjudicated structure covers, for a single directed duty used as a mixin: deontic core and violability, obligor/obligee/beneficiary/enforcement roles, obligated action and subject matter, antecedent conditions and ODRL-form constraint expression, due time, recurrence, limitation and survival, an explicit lifecycle state model with dual timestamps, fulfilment with acceptance and evidence, non-performance with excuse, cure and remedy, legal basis, authority and jurisdiction, stewardship, provenance, confidentiality and retention, composition, transfer, plurality, and standards alignment — plus the imported XACML/HL7 obligation-sense crosswalk and the UNIDROIT cure/additional-period operation. Grounding is limited to the cited primary standards; service-level-objective structure and obligations-register operations remain declared gaps. No claim of jurisdictional, deontic-logical or universal completeness is made.

checklist.notes: Identity priority, scheme, standing-versus-occurrence granularity, versioning by supersession and an explicit deduplication match key; explicitly excludes dates and descriptive attribute combinations as identifiers. Grounded in ODRL uid requirements, LegalRuleML statement identification and FIBO commitment structure.

Explicit state set, transition matrix, derived-versus-asserted state basis, terminal states, authorised reopening and transient-versus-terminal breach for maintenance obligations. Grounded in the ODRL fulfilment test, LegalRuleML Violation/Compliance and the achievement/maintenance distinction from AAAI 2021.

Obligor, obligee, beneficiary, auxiliary and enforcing roles; correlative right link; parent-child decomposition; ordering and reciprocal dependency; plurality with joint and several liability and contribution. Grounded in FIBO party roles, LegalRuleML bearer/auxiliary party and UNIDROIT Chapters 6 and 11.

Due basis distinguishing fixed time, obligor-chosen period, reasonable time and event-derived deadlines; recurrence, grace, notice lead times, limitation, survival and enforceability windows; all instants RFC 3339 with explicit offset and separated event and observation times.

Generating activity, attributed agent, derived-from links to the source clause, extraction method and confidence, creation and ingestion timestamps, and a chained tamper-evident audit trail. Aligned to PROV-O starting-point and qualified terms.

Record owner separated from obligor; monitoring assignment, review cadence, attestation and escalation path; delegated performance with retained accountability expressed through PROV-O delegation. Register-upkeep grounding from ISO 37301 is scope-level only.

Constraint consistency and unsatisfiability checks, non-empty collection refinement checks, null-operation checks on action refinement, role disjointness, cycle detection on dependencies, and conformance claims gated on dated validator evidence. Grounded in the ODRL Validator and Evaluator roles.

Deny-by-default with scoped grants across bundle, layer, finding and artifact; party self-access, supervisory and judicial exceptions, and a narrowed evaluator scope that excludes free text and personal data. Every read and grant is logged.

Retention triggered by discharge or end of enforceability and justified by the limitation determination; legal hold; erasure reconciled against the legal-obligation and legal-claims exceptions; hard deletion prohibited in-window with tombstoning to preserve referential integrity. Grounded in GDPR Articles 5(1)(e), 6(1)(c), 17 and 30 and UNIDROIT Chapter 10.

Crosswalk with mapping relations, pinned target versions, recorded divergences, conflict-resolution strategy, profile identification and the requirement to halt on unrecognised profiles; conformance separated from alignment.
Obligation, prohibition, permission and right typed explicitly, with violation polarity and the SBVR deontic-versus-alethic filter that keeps definitional necessities out of the register.
Suspensive and resolutive conditions, detachment timestamps and evidence, duties pending the condition, interference findings, and ODRL constraint and logical-constraint expression form.

Fulfilment test as constraint satisfaction plus exercise of the refined action, acceptance as a separate step, discharge modes, and evidence with issuer, validity interval, integrity proof and revocation status aligned to VC 2.0.

Non-performance covering non-delivery, defect and lateness; declaration authority and notice; materiality; excuse grounds; cure periods; and consequence, remedy and penalty obligations that recurse onto this model.
Quantity owed, partial performance, cumulative fulfilled and outstanding quantities, and input- or output-based measure of progress from IFRS 15, with penalty formulae and caps.

Thresholds, tolerances and measurement windows are modelled generically because the cloud SLA standard normally relied on (ISO/IEC 19086-1) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. Only UNIDROIT 5.1.6 reasonable-quality grounding is primary; treat the SLO shape as unsupported structure pending retrieval.

Register upkeep, currency and accessibility requirements rest on the ISO 37301 committee scope statement only; the normative clause text is paywalled and was not read, so review cadence, escalation and register completeness requirements are presented as practice, not as cited normative requirements.
Place of performance with stated-versus-default indicator, jurisdictional territory and subject-matter extent, and ODRL spatial operands. Grounded in UNIDROIT 6.1.6 and LegalRuleML Jurisdiction.

Place of performance is a reference into a location or party model rather than a geometry; no coordinate reference system, precision or topology requirement arises from the sources for a general obligation mixin.

Integrity digests chained across append-only logs, quarantine of artefacts failing integrity checks, verification of external proofs without re-signing, and authority requirements for state assertions.
Personal data flag, lawful basis, minimised evaluator access, and separately reportable access to personal data. Grounded in GDPR Articles 6(1)(c) and 30.

Assignment of rights, transfer of duties, delegation of performance and novation, each with consent or notice requirements, release status and an explicit identity continuity rule. Grounded in UNIDROIT Chapter 9.

known_omissions: ISO/IEC 19086-1 (cloud SLA framework, service level objectives and service qualitative objectives) could not be retrieved; the standard's page returned HTTP 403. The performance-standard finding therefore lacks the primary grounding that would normally define threshold, metric and measurement-window structure.
The normative text of ISO 37301:2021 is paywalled; only the ISO/TC 309 committee scope statement was read. Obligations-register requirements are therefore treated as gap-level support.

Multiagent commitment-protocol literature that formalises the operations create, cancel, release, delegate and assign over C(debtor, creditor, antecedent, consequent) could not be machine-read (the AAMAS commitment-alignment PDF failed to parse). The state model is grounded in ODRL, LegalRuleML and UNIDROIT, with the achievement-versus-maintenance distinction taken from the AAAI 2021 abstract only; the finer-grained commitment operations are deliberately not asserted.

The OMG SBVR specification page yielded title, version and date but not the clause text on deontic and alethic modality; the distinction as used here is supported at the level of SBVR's stated purpose plus secondary commentary, so the violability filter is a weaker claim than the ODRL and LegalRuleML groundings.
Insolvency effects on obligations — automatic stay, set-off on insolvency, subordination and rescission of preferences — are not modelled and would materially change enforceability.
Tax, prudential and sector-specific statutory obligation catalogues are not enumerated; only GDPR is used as a worked statutory example.

Non-Western and non-commercial obligation frameworks (Shariah-compliant structures, customary and community obligations, family-law duties) are not addressed; the model's grounding is commercial and regulatory.

Distributed-ledger or self-executing settlement semantics are treated as an interface projection and are not modelled; automated execution introduces determinism and finality questions this model does not answer.
Negotiation and pre-contractual commitments (letters of intent, memoranda of understanding, comfort letters) are not distinguished from binding commitments beyond the violability filter.
Aggregate and portfolio-level views — exposure across obligations, netting, and covenant baskets — are out of scope; this model describes one obligation at a time.
FIBO FND Law LegalCapacity contingent-obligation and condition-precedent properties were only snippet-searched, not fetched as a full ontology, so clause-linkage details are a gap.
Assignment, delegation and novation of obligations are not specified in the fetched UNIDROIT chapter 7 section 1; likely belong to a sibling transfer/novation model.
Joint and several liability multiplicity is asked but not grounded in a primary multiplicity scheme beyond FIBO party-role cardinality.
Prescription, limitation periods and death/incapacity of the obligor lack primary support in the fetched set.
CISG Article 33 (time of performance) is the acknowledged inspiration for UNIDROIT 6.1.1 but was not fetched.
ISO 37301 compliance-management obligations and ISO 22600-2 (cited by HL7) were not fetched as primary texts.
Smart-contract oracle fulfilment, Islamic finance consideration rules, and criminal-law duties are out of the fetched corpus.
DPROD dutyState is an emerging profile, not W3C ODRL core; using it as canonical state without a Dimension declaration would be over-claim.
Hohfeld correlatives are treated only via LegalRuleML Right and FIBO reciprocity, not via a jurisprudence primary text.
conflicts: ODRL requires exactly one target Asset on a Permission and a Prohibition, and models actions as operations on assets. Many legal and regulatory obligations (file a return, maintain insurance, appoint an officer) have no asset. ODRL's Duty allows zero-or-one target, so duties remain expressible, but any projection that routes obligations through permissions will misfit; recorded as a divergence rather than resolved.

ODRL forbids a consequence Duty from itself carrying a consequence, and forbids a remedy from referring to a Duty that includes a consequence. Legal escalation chains are open-ended (interest on unpaid damages, penalties on unpaid penalties). This model recurses onto itself for secondary obligations and therefore cannot round-trip deep escalation chains through ODRL without flattening; the flattening strategy must be recorded.

LegalRuleML models a Right as a Permission to a bearer implying obligations on auxiliary parties, while FIBO models a Commitment as a promise giving rise to both an obligation and a reciprocal right. The modelling unit differs — a normative statement versus a promise — so a one-to-one mapping between LegalRuleML Right and FIBO Commitment must not be assumed.

The IFRS 15 sense of performance obligation is narrower than the legal sense: it covers only promises to transfer distinct goods or services to a customer, and obligations falling outside it are addressed by other standards. Treating the accounting flag as a general obligation classifier would misclassify most regulatory and internal obligations.

ODRL distinguishes a policy-level obligation from a duty attached as a pre-condition of a permission, with different fulfilment consequences. Collapsing both into a single obligation field loses the distinction between a freestanding duty and a duty that gates an entitlement.

RFC 3339 requires an explicit offset, but many legal deadlines are stated in local civil time with a business-day convention and no offset. Canonicalising to a UTC instant at capture destroys legally relevant information; this model retains both representations, which means the canonical instant alone is not authoritative for deadline disputes.

ODRL requires a processing system to stop when it does not recognise a profile identifier, whereas obligation registers commonly need best-effort ingestion of partially understood external policies. Silent partial processing would breach the ODRL requirement; the model therefore requires an explicit halt-and-quarantine rather than lenient parsing.
ODRL fulfilment is binary exercise of an action; UNIDROIT non-performance includes defective and late performance of an otherwise exercised action. Do not collapse these tests.
IAS 37 recognises constructive obligations; US GAAP Topic 450 generally does not under the same model. Overlay fields must not be overwritten across bases.
XACML/HL7/FHIR 'obligation' is a mandated operation or conformance behaviour beside an access or data-handling decision, not a contractual Duty.
ODRL consequence keeps the original duty required; some commercial practices treat liquidated damages as substituting for performance. Record the rule actually adopted.
LegalRuleML Prohibition as [OBL]-p versus ODRL Prohibition as a disjoint Rule subclass: forbearance modelling will not round-trip without an explicit map.
IFRS 15 performance-obligation satisfaction (control transfer) is not the same as ODRL Duty fulfilment or UNIDROIT due performance.
regional_assumptions: The UNIDROIT Principles are soft law: they apply where the parties choose them, where they supplement an international instrument, or as gap-fillers. Their rules on best efforts, conditions, place and currency of performance, force majeure, hardship, assignment, limitation and plurality are used here as a well-attested reference frame, not as universally binding law.

Limitation periods, survival rules and the enforceability of penalty and liquidated-damages clauses vary materially by jurisdiction; several common-law systems restrict penalty clauses that civil-law systems permit. Specific durations and enforceability outcomes must be determined per governing law and are deliberately not asserted here.

GDPR-derived retention, erasure and lawful-basis structure applies to personal data within EU and EEA scope. Other regimes impose different retention floors and erasure rights, so the retention finding's mechanics are portable but its specific bases are not.

IFRS 15 applies where IFRS Accounting Standards are used; converged but non-identical national standards exist elsewhere, and jurisdictions on local GAAP may define performance obligations differently or not at all.

Business-day conventions, public holidays and civil-time offsets are jurisdiction-specific and are referenced from a calendar model rather than defined here; deadline computation is only as correct as that reference.

Notice service rules, including what counts as effective service and when it takes effect, are jurisdiction-specific; the model records service evidence and instants but does not assert validity of service.
UNIDROIT Principles are an international commercial-law restatement, not domestic mandatory law; local civil-code or common-law rules may add consideration, privity or formality requirements.
IAS 37/IFRS 15 overlays assume IFRS reporting; US GAAP and other GAAPs differ on constructive obligations and contingency thresholds.
LegalRuleML encodings are jurisdiction-neutral carriers of jurisdiction-specific norms; jurisdiction-code is an annotation, not a world-law identifier.
ODRL is a web policy language widely used for rights, not a substitute for private-law obligation in courts.
HL7/FHIR obligation codes reflect health-interoperability practice and must not be generalised as legal duties.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample — commitment with no identified beneficiary. FIBO recognises a commitment at large made without direct involvement of potential beneficiaries. The model therefore makes the obligee reference optional (0..n) and adds an explicit directedness code, rather than requiring a counterparty as most contract-centric designs do.

Counterexample — negative obligation. A duty to refrain is violated by performing the act, not by omitting it. A single boolean 'fulfilled' flag would be meaningless here, so violation polarity is a required element and forbearance is flagged on the action, keeping prohibition semantics from being silently coerced into obligation semantics.

Counterexample — obligation with no asset. Statutory duties such as appointing a data protection officer or responding within one month have no target asset. Target references are therefore 0..n with an explicit assertion available for the target-free case, and the ODRL asset-targeting divergence is recorded rather than papered over.

Counterexample — maintenance obligation. A duty to keep insurance in force is not discharged by a single act and cannot be modelled by a due date plus a completion flag. The achievement/maintenance axis is a required classification and the state model requires transient lapse to be distinguishable from terminal breach.

Counterexample — obligation that is owed but unenforceable. Limitation and survival are modelled separately from discharge, so an obligation can be substantively outstanding while time-barred, which a simple open/closed state model cannot express.

Rejected structure — a priority, urgency or workload layer. Attractive for operations, but these are attributes of the work item that discharges the obligation, not of the duty itself; admitting them would duplicate the task model and make obligation records vary with staffing.

Rejected structure — a smart-contract or automation-execution layer. Self-execution is a property of a projection and an interface, not of the obligation's semantics; including it would violate the format-neutrality requirement and embed finality assumptions the sources do not support.

Rejected structure — an accounting recognition and provisioning layer. IFRS 15's boundary makes clear that recognition and measurement are a separate discipline; the model carries only the performance-obligation flag and the distinctness assessment, and refers the rest out.

Conflation test — obligation versus requirement or control. A compliance requirement in a register and an instantiated duty on a named bearer are different objects with different lifecycles; the model describes one entry and explicitly excludes control design and assurance results, keeping the register aggregation in a sibling model.

Overreach test — conformance claims. Every alignment is stated as a mapping with a relation and recorded conflicts, and the service layer forbids asserting conformance without a dated validation report, so no node in this structure claims standard conformance on the strength of resemblance alone.

Support test — every layer traced to primary sources. Two dimensions failed this test and are marked as gaps rather than presented as canonical: service-level objective structure (ISO/IEC 19086-1 unreachable) and obligations-register operations (ISO 37301 clause text paywalled).
If an English label 'obligation' is used as a join key across ODRL, XACML and IAS 37, legally distinct senses will be merged; deontic-kind-code is the falsifier.
If fulfilment is stored as a boolean without performance-quality-code, defective and late performance required by UNIDROIT 7.1.1 become invisible.
If due dates are used as identifiers or stored as timezone-naive dates, overdue evaluation is not reproducible across regions.
If consequence duties replace the original duty by default, the instance is not ODRL-compatible even if labelled as such.
If FHIR SHALL-handle-field codes are treated as contractual commitments, healthcare conformance will be misread as legal liability.
If IAS 37 recognition is taken as proof that no obligation exists when outflow is not probable, deontic duties will disappear from operations while still binding at law.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently arrived at mixin, and the base scope statement, ten boundary notes and explicit out-of-scope list draw complete lines against the agreement instrument, party master data, the policy/rule container, task execution, payment and settlement mechanics, dispute management, control registers and accounting recognition. The base also passes the definitional/alethic filter (SBVR) that keeps non-violable necessities out of the register. The only boundary pressure in this adjudication is the imported access-control and conformance obligation sense, which is admitted as a crosswalk alignment entry only, leaving the base exclusion of decision-point and evaluation infrastructure intact.

decisions.rationale: The base carries ten boundary notes, an explicit out-of-scope list and adversarial counterexamples (commitment at large, negative duty, asset-free statutory duty, maintenance duty, owed-but-time-barred duty) that close the model edges. The alternative's seven notes are sound but leave party roles, stewardship, provenance and retention thin. Node count was not decisive; edge completeness was.

Both providers independently classified the entry as a mixin attachable to contracts, statutes, licences, orders, policies and unilateral commitments, and neither structure carries instrument formation, party identity or ledger semantics that would force a standalone entity.

Tier-1 primary grounding for two obligation homonyms absent from the base crosswalk; admitted as mapping and sense-disambiguation only, with the source finding's access and retention material dropped as duplicative of base access-and-retention.

decisions.concept: IAS 37 provision recognition and measurement overlay
decisions.rationale: The base explicitly out-of-scopes accounting recognition and measurement and draws a boundary note to Liability/Provision. Importing provision amount, risk adjustment, discounting and onerous-contract testing would reopen a deliberately closed edge and duplicate a sibling financial-reporting model.

decisions.concept: IAS 37 legal versus constructive obligation classification
decisions.rationale: Adjacent to but not identical with the base external-versus-voluntary origin axis from ISO 37301. Deciding whether constructive obligation is an origin class of the duty or only a recognition trigger requires primary clause text neither provider read, so it is not bolted onto obligation-typology on inference.

Tier-3 non-primary profile, and the source provider itself flags adopting it as canonical as an over-claim. The base lifecycle-state-machine is grounded in the ODRL fulfilment test, LegalRuleML Violation/Compliance indications and the achievement/maintenance distinction, which is stronger support.

Place and currency of performance already sit in base subject-and-place, and ordering with reciprocal dependency in finding-composition-and-dependency; importing the finding would fragment place of performance across two nodes. Its one unique element, withholding performance, is deferred to research instead.

Base antecedent-and-detachment plus constraint-expression already carry suspensive and resolutive conditions, detachment evidence and timestamping, improper interference, and the full ODRL Constraint and LogicalConstraint expression form including andSequence ordering.

Base excuse-remedy-consequence already carries the ODRL consequence and remedy nesting prohibitions, LegalRuleML PenaltyStatement and Reparation, cure periods, penalty caps, and the recursion of secondary duties back onto this model as obligations in their own right.

The base already asserts ODRL Validator and Evaluator grounding in its validation checklist dimension and covers competent issuer and evidence sufficiency in fulfilment-evidence; importing the combined evidence finding would create a second evidence node for one extra distinction.

The base recognises cure as a question but exposes no operation between declaring non-performance and applying remedy, so the suspension of inconsistent remedies during an additional period is currently unreachable; grounded in a tier-1 primary source.

Enforcing ObligationExpressions on a Permit or Deny decision is decision-point infrastructure, which the base out-of-scopes. The XACML sense enters as a crosswalk entry only, never as an operation of this mixin.

Follows the same boundary as the rejected IAS 37 overlay: applying provision versus contingent-liability tests is a financial-reporting operation on some obligations, not an operation of the deontic record itself.

Base transition-state applies permitted transitions with authority, basis, event time and observation time, and fulfilment-and-acceptance already enumerates discharge modes including substitute performance, set-off, waiver, release and expiry.

decisions.disposition: recorded as declared divergence, not resolved
decisions.rationale: Both providers independently find that LegalRuleML obligation-of-a-negated-act and the ODRL disjoint Prohibition subclass will not round-trip. The base already records violation polarity and a divergence list, so synthesis keeps this as a crosswalk conflict rather than choosing a winner without primary authority to do so.

The two providers scatter access, retention, validation and interoperability service concerns across different bundles; merging them onto the base's single service surface prevents two competing access-control and retention narratives coexisting in one published model.

publicationHolds: Live-URL and version-pin verification for all fourteen base sources plus the two imported ones (XACML 3.0, HL7 FHIR obligation codes) before any citation is published.

FIBO source conflict: the base pins spec.edmcouncil.org Agreements and Contracts at 'master/latest retrieved 2026-08-23' while the other provider pins raw.githubusercontent.com at versionIRI 20260601. Resolve to one dated release IRI before publication.

UNIDROIT edition pin: the base cites the 2016 black-letter PDF, while the imported cure and additional-period function derives from a 2010 Chapter 7 Section 1 page. Confirm 2016 numbering for Articles 7.1.1 to 7.1.5 before citing them.

Multi-profile domain validation: exercise the mixin against a contract clause, a statutory or regulatory duty, a court or administrative order, an internal voluntary commitment and an access-control or conformance obligation before claiming the alignment holds.

Performance-standard finding remains partially supported: ISO/IEC 19086-1 returned HTTP 403, so thresholds, metrics and measurement windows must be published as generic structure explicitly labelled as lacking primary grounding.

ISO 37301 normative clause text is paywalled and only the committee scope statement was read; register upkeep, review cadence and escalation must be published as practice, not as cited normative requirements.

Confirm the imported XACML and FHIR sense alignment is published as a crosswalk entry only and does not reopen the base exclusion of access-control decision points and their evaluation infrastructure.
No conformance claim to ODRL, LegalRuleML, FIBO, IFRS 15, XACML or FHIR may be published without a dated validation report; alignment relations only until then.
deferredResearch: UNIDROIT 7.1.2: non-performance caused by the other party's act or by a risk it bears, and whether the base needs an explicit interference and risk-allocation defence distinct from the existing condition-interference question.

UNIDROIT 7.1.3 withholding of performance in reciprocal obligations (simultaneous versus consecutive tender) as a distinct pre-remedy state of an unperformed duty, currently absent from both the composition and the non-performance layers.

UNIDROIT 7.2.1 and 7.2.2 limits on specific performance (impossibility, unreasonable burden, reasonable cover from another source, exclusively personal character) and whether they belong to this mixin or to a remedies sibling model.
Whether the IAS 37 constructive obligation and the ISO 37301 voluntary commitment are the same origin axis; requires the normative clause text of both, neither of which was read by either provider.

Multiagent commitment operations (create, cancel, release, delegate, assign) over C(debtor, creditor, antecedent, consequent): the AAMAS commitment-alignment PDF failed to parse, so the finer-grained operations remain unasserted in the state model.

Insolvency effects on enforceability — automatic stay, set-off on insolvency, subordination and rescission of preferences — listed as a base known omission and material to the limitation and survival findings.
DPROD Duty profile status and whether any Dimension declares it, before its Pending/Active/Fulfilled/Violated vocabulary could ever be referenced as more than a third-party profile.
