findings.inline_only_rationale: Designation is descriptive inline metadata carried on the record; no separate artifact is produced by titling, and treating a title list as an artifact would invite its use as an identifier, which the identity rule forbids.

layers.name: Documentary form and classification
layers.description: The genre of the record and its placement in a business classification scheme and archival aggregation, which drive the rules that later apply to it.

findings.name: Documentary form and genre
findings.description: The documentary form the record takes (contract, certificate, invoice, minutes, licence) typed against a controlled vocabulary, and the rules that follow from that form.

findings.name: Business classification and aggregation membership
findings.description: Filing of the record under a classification class and its membership in aggregations, with the boundary to the archival aggregation model held explicitly.

bundles.name: Content, versions and manifestations
bundles.description: What the record says, the immutable states its content passes through, and the format-specific and carrier-specific realisations that make it readable.
bundles.rationale: PREMIS distinguishes Intellectual Entity, Representation, File and Bitstream, and RiC-O separates record resource from instantiation; collapsing these layers makes format migration indistinguishable from content change and destroys the evidentiary chain.

layers.name: Content and components
layers.description: The body of the record, its structural parts, attachments and the properties that must survive any transformation.

findings.name: Content structure, components and completeness
findings.description: Which parts make up the complete record, which are essential to its meaning, and how completeness is verified at capture.

layers.name: Versions and instantiations
layers.description: The immutable version chain of content states and the multiple physical or digital instantiations that realise each state.

findings.name: Version chain and immutability
findings.description: How a content state is fixed, how versions supersede and amend one another, and the prohibition on editing an issued version in place.

findings.name: Instantiation, copy and original status
findings.description: Format-specific and carrier-specific realisations of a version, and the legal distinction between the original of record, duplicates, certified copies and extracts.

findings.name: Supersession between records
findings.description: Dublin Core replaces/isReplacedBy model a related resource that supplants another. A new record may supersede an older record (policy, specification, licence) without being a version of the same identity. Supersession does not by itself authorize destruction of the replaced record; disposition remains a separate control.

layers.name: Format, fixity and preservation
layers.description: Technical identification of instantiations, the environment needed to render them, and the integrity and preservation controls applied over time.

findings.name: Format identification and rendering environment
findings.description: How each instantiation's format is identified against registries and what software and hardware environment is required to render it.

findings.name: Fixity and preservation actions
findings.description: Baseline digests, verification history, declared preservation level and the actions applied to keep instantiations readable, including those that change bytes.

bundles.name: Agency, authority and issuance
bundles.description: Who is responsible for the record, who owns and who keeps it, and the act of issuing it under a mandate and entering it into a register.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 makes assigned responsibility a precondition of trustworthy recordkeeping, RiC-O models Mandate and Agent as distinct contextual entities, and eIDAS makes the issuing legal person material to legal effect; ownership must be separable from custody.

layers.name: Agents, ownership and custody
layers.description: Role-qualified references to the agents who made, approved, own and keep the record.

findings.name: Authorship and responsibility roles
findings.description: Who authored, contributed to, approved and was addressed by the record, expressed as role-qualified references rather than embedded agent descriptions.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Agent attributes are governed by the person and organization models; this finding stores only role-qualified references, and the artifacts that evidence responsibility are the signature object and the event history recorded in other findings.

findings.name: Ownership, custody and stewardship
findings.description: The separation between the record owner and the custodian or registrar acting on the owner's behalf, and the terms limiting custodial power.

layers.name: Issuance and registration
layers.description: The act of issuing the record under a mandate in a jurisdiction, and its entry into a custodial or public register.

findings.name: Issuance, mandate and register entry
findings.description: The legal basis and jurisdiction under which the record was issued, and the register entry that anchors it in a custodial system.

bundles.name: Authenticity and evidentiary value
bundles.description: Why the record can be relied on: signatures and seals bound to fixed content, trusted timestamps, dated validation outcomes, derivation provenance and an unbroken chain of custody.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 makes authenticity and integrity defining characteristics of an authoritative record, eIDAS attaches legal effect to signature and timestamp tiers, and PROV-O and C2PA supply the derivation and binding structures; validity is time-dependent and must be recorded as evidence, not asserted as a flag.

layers.name: Signatures, seals and validation evidence
layers.description: Signature and seal objects bound to specific content, the timestamps that fix their moment, and the dated results of validating them.

findings.name: Signature, seal and attestation
findings.description: Signatures, seals and attestations applied to a version or instantiation, their assurance tier, their signatory and exactly what content each binds.

findings.name: Timestamping and validation evidence
findings.description: Trusted time-stamp tokens proving existence at a time, validation outcomes recorded with their own validation instant and policy, and the renewal of evidence before algorithms weaken.

findings.name: Authoritative record characteristics
findings.description: ISO 23081 states that metadata must support assertions of integrity, authenticity, reliability and usability over time in business context. ISO 15489 requires records to remain authoritative through those characteristics: authentic (what it purports to be, created or sent by the purported agent at the purported time), reliable (trusted full and accurate content of the transaction), integrity (complete and unaltered), usable (locatable, retrievable, presentable, interpretable). These are assessed properties with evidence, not decorative flags.

layers.name: Provenance and chain of custody
layers.description: Where the record came from and who held it at every moment between creation and now.

findings.name: Derivation and provenance graph
findings.description: The activities that generated the record, the sources it derives from, and the agents associated with each generating activity.

findings.name: Chain of custody and hand-over
findings.description: The gapless sequence of custody intervals, hand-over receipts and integrity checks that allows the record to be relied on as evidence.

bundles.name: State, time and recordkeeping control
bundles.description: The status the record is in, the events that moved it there, the time anchors it carries, and the retention, hold and disposition regime that decides its end.
bundles.rationale: NARA's universal requirements organise records systems by lifecycle from capture through disposal and transfer, MoReq2010 requires an event history on every entity and separates disposal scheduling from disposal holding, and RFC 3339 makes explicit offsets mandatory; state, time and disposition are one control problem.

layers.name: Status, lifecycle events and time
layers.description: Controlled status values, the append-only history of what happened, and the distinct time anchors the record carries.

findings.name: Record status and permitted transitions
findings.description: The controlled status vocabulary, which transitions are permitted from each state, who may authorise them, and how withdrawal differs from destruction.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Status is inline state carried directly on the record and required in every projection including existence-level views; its evidence is the event history artifact in the adjacent finding, so a duplicate artifact would be a second source of truth.

findings.name: Lifecycle events and audit trail
findings.description: The append-only history of everything done to and with the record, using controlled event types with actor, outcome, event time and separately recorded observation time.

findings.name: Temporal anchors and validity periods
findings.description: The distinct time anchors a record carries — created, issued, effective, expiry, received, observed — their precision, and the rule separating event time from ingestion time.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Time anchors are inline scalar values attached to the record, its versions and its events; the artifacts that carry temporal evidence are the trusted time-stamp token and the event history, both defined in other findings.

findings.name: Document versus captured record
findings.description: ISO 15489 applies to records regardless of structure or form and treats capture into a records system as the act that places identified information under records controls. RiC-CM defines a Record as discrete information content formed and inscribed, at least once, on any persistent recoverable carrier by an agent in the course of activity. US 36 CFR 1220.18 / 44 U.S.C. 3301 additionally excludes extra copies kept only for reference, library or museum materials for exhibit, and personal files. This model stores a record-status on the object: document-not-captured, captured-record, nonrecord-copy, or jurisdiction-specific Federal-record, rather than splitting into two meta-models.

layers.name: Retention, disposition and holds
layers.description: The authorised schedule that decides the record's fate, the suspensions that override it, and the evidence that survives execution.

findings.name: Retention class and disposition authority
findings.description: The retention class assigned to the record, the instrument authorising it, the trigger that starts the clock and the action due at the end.

findings.name: Holds and disposition suspension
findings.description: Legal holds and other suspensions that override retention schedules until explicitly released, and the mechanism that prevents automated disposal of held records.

findings.name: Disposition execution and surviving evidence
findings.description: Carrying out destruction, transfer or permanent retention, and the evidence and tombstone that outlive the record itself.

bundles.name: Access, rights and interoperability
bundles.description: Who may see what, on what legal footing content may be reused, and how the record and its evidence move between systems without losing meaning.
bundles.rationale: NARA's transfer guidance makes access restriction status a mandatory transfer element, DCMI supplies accessRights, license and rightsHolder, and IANA and format registries govern the value space for exchange; access and interoperability are governed together because every projection is an access decision.

layers.name: Access, security marking and rights
layers.description: Markings and decisions controlling who may read the record, and the intellectual-property and personal-data constraints on reuse.

findings.name: Access conditions and security marking
findings.description: The security marking and access restriction status carried by the record, the statutory regime behind them, and the recorded decisions on individual requests.

findings.name: Rights, licensing and personal data
findings.description: Who holds rights in the content, under what licence it may be reused, and what personal data within it constrains processing and release.

layers.name: Interoperability and exchange
layers.description: Declared mappings to external metadata standards and the packaging and projection rules for moving records between systems.

findings.name: Metadata alignment and conformance evidence
findings.description: Which external standards the record's metadata is mapped to, where mappings lose information, and what evidence is required before any conformance claim is made.

findings.name: Exchange packaging and projections
findings.description: How a record and its evidence are packaged for transfer or publication, and how each projection deliberately omits parts without breaking reconstructability.

model.name: Organization
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, classify, register, operate on and reason about any organization — company, NGO, cooperative, institution, public body, community or informal collective — independently of any storage or interface projection.
model.scope_statement: WM-ORG-001 models the organization as an externally addressable actor: its designations, scheme-qualified identifiers, legal form and activity classification, declared purpose and scale, formation and registry standing, lifecycle and succession, external control/ownership and official representation, physical and electronic presence, and the provenance, quality, access and interoperability governance of the organization record itself. Internal composition (units, teams), person-level records, employment relations and constitutive rule detail are delegated to sibling models. Storage in JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MongoDB or exposure over MCP or HTTP are projections of this semantics, never part of it.
in_scope: Names and designations over time, including language, script and transliteration variants
Scheme-qualified identifiers (LEI, national registration number, EUID, VAT/tax IDs, DUNS, GLN) and internal canonical keys
Entity legal form, entity category/subcategory and legal personality
Activity and sector classification (NACE, ISIC, national schemes) and statistical-unit alignment
Declared purpose, object clause, non-profit status and scale indicators
Formation act, registry entries, registration authority and registered standing
Entity status vs registration status, recurring filing and renewal obligations
Lifecycle events, succession, continuity and lineage across mergers, divisions and conversions
External group, ownership, beneficial-ownership and control relationships as endpoints
Official organizational roles and authorised representation at organization level
Registered office, operating sites, branches and electronic addresses/channels
Record provenance, corroboration level, data quality, disclosure classification, retention and standard crosswalks
out_of_scope: Internal organizational units, divisions and departments (WM-ORG-002)
Teams and operational groupings (WM-ORG-003)
Natural persons as subjects, including officer and beneficial-owner person records
Employment, appointment and contractor relations as person-to-organization records
Full constitutive rule text, bylaws, powers and decision procedures (charter model)
The public register as an institution, its governance and its own lifecycle
Financial statements, tax positions, products, services and contracts
Physical facility, property and premises detail beyond the presence pointer
Trademark and brand rights over names
Access-grant issuance and stewardship mechanics (service models)

boundary_notes.distinction: W3C ORG separates FormalOrganization (legally recognised, can hold external identifiers and be a party) from OrganizationalUnit, which exists only within a larger organization. Test: if the subject can independently hold a registry entry or a scheme-issued identifier, it belongs here; otherwise it is a unit. Branches are the hard case — a branch may hold its own LEI (EntityCategory BRANCH) yet is not a separate legal person, so it is modelled here as a categorised organization record linked by IS_INTERNATIONAL_BRANCH_OF rather than as an internal unit.

A team is an operational grouping with no external legal or registry standing and no scheme-qualified identifier. Teams are contained instances, never subjects of registration, standing or succession findings in this model.

Eurostat's business-register recommendations treat the legal unit and the statistical enterprise as different units: an enterprise may combine several legal units, and enterprise-group boundaries follow control, not legal personality. This model's subject is the organization-as-actor; statistical-unit membership is recorded as a classification alignment, never as identity, and must not be used to merge or split organization records.

GLEIF EntityCategory SOLE_PROPRIETOR recognises a business subject whose legal person is a natural person. The natural person remains a separate subject in the person model; this model holds only the business-facing record and the link.

Registration authorities are themselves organizations and are enumerated in a governed registry (GLEIF RA list, 1,050+ registers, 232 jurisdictions). This model stores a reference to the authority code and the entry, not the register's own model content.

BODS separates entity records, person records and relationship records. Only entity records and the organization-side endpoints of relationship records are in scope; person records and their personal data are delegated, because they carry different privacy, access and retention obligations.

W3C ORG hasSite/hasRegisteredSite point at Site, which is itself a locatable thing. This model holds the presence assertion (kind, validity, role of the location) and references the place model for geometry, building and postal-normalisation detail.

GLEIF EntityCategory FUND with IS_SUBFUND_OF, IS_FEEDER_TO and IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY shows that fund vehicles are organization-like subjects whose 'control' semantics are management and umbrella membership rather than ownership. They are in scope as categorised organizations but their investment semantics are not modelled here.

A large share of organizations (community groups, clubs, unincorporated associations, informal collectives) have no registry entry and no scheme identifier. The registration and standing bundle must therefore be optional, and identity must be able to rest on an adopting-Dimension UUID/ULID. Claiming registry-backed identity for such subjects is a modelling error, not a data gap.

functions.name: Resolve organization identifier
functions.description: Resolve a scheme-qualified identifier to the canonical organization record, returning a minimal profile and the corroboration level of the answer.
outputs: minimal profile fields for the requested projection
preconditions: The scheme designator exists in the identifier scheme catalogue
The requesting agent holds access to the requested projection
The identifier passes the scheme's syntax and check-character rule
effects: Emits a resolution audit entry with agent, scheme, value and timestamp
Records a negative-resolution entry when no record matches, to avoid repeated lookups

functions.name: Ingest registry extract
functions.description: Ingest a point-in-time extract from a named register, storing it as an immutable artifact and deriving field-level assertions with provenance.
preconditions: The register code exists in the governed registration-authority list
The extract carries or is assigned a content digest
The licence permits the intended storage and projection
effects: Creates an immutable extract artifact with digest and retrieval metadata
Appends provenance nodes attributing each derived assertion to the register
Raises conflict observations where derived values disagree with held values

functions.name: Assert lifecycle event
functions.description: Record a lifecycle event affecting the organization, with separate effective, authority-recording and observation times, affected fields and validation documents.
preconditions: The event type exists in the governed event type list
The asserting agent is authorised to assert events for this organization
Effective date is not later than the observation timestamp unless a future-dated filing is explicitly flagged
effects: Appends an entry to the append-only lifecycle event journal
Updates affected fields and retains the prior values as a versioned snapshot
Triggers re-evaluation of standing and obligation schedules

functions.name: Evaluate succession continuity
functions.description: Decide whether a transition preserved organizational identity or created a new subject, and write the resulting lineage edges.
preconditions: The transition event exists in the lifecycle journal
A continuity rule set version is declared and retrievable
At least one predecessor is identified by a canonical key
effects: Writes lineage edges keyed by predecessor, successor and causing event
Marks identifiers as carried over or lapsed on the affected records
Records the decision, deciding agent and rule version in the resolution decision log

functions.name: Reconcile duplicate organization records
functions.description: Compare candidate records, record the comparison evidence and confidence, and execute a merge, split or explicit non-match decision with a reversible tombstone.
preconditions: All candidates are readable by the deciding agent
Upstream duplicate or annulled status has been checked
A rollback path exists for the chosen action
effects: Writes an entry to the entity resolution decision log with evidence and confidence
Creates tombstones that keep retired keys resolvable to the survivor
Records explicit non-matches so the comparison is not repeated

functions.name: Assign or migrate activity classification
functions.description: Assign an activity code under a named scheme revision, or migrate an existing assignment to a newer revision using a published correspondence table.
outputs: activity code assignment with scheme version
preconditions: The target scheme revision is available in the local reference set
A correspondence table exists for the requested migration
The principality criterion is declared
effects: Writes the assignment with an explicit scheme revision
Retains the prior assignment with its revision rather than overwriting it
Flags migrations whose mapping is not one-to-one for review

functions.name: Record control or ownership relationship
functions.description: Create or update a relationship record between the organization and another party, with typed periods, quantifiers, interests and, where applicable, a reporting exception.
outputs: exception reason where no counterparty can be reported
preconditions: Both endpoints resolve, or the counterparty is explicitly marked unspecified with a reason
The relationship or interest type exists in the governed list
Beneficial-ownership flags are set only where the interested party is a natural person
effects: Writes a standalone relationship record with its own registration metadata
Records the source type, retrieval time and asserting party per statement
Records an exception reason and review date instead of omitting an unreportable link

functions.name: Evaluate record standing and obligations
functions.description: Recompute entity status, record registration status and the obligation schedule from held observations, flagging staleness and imminent lapse.
outputs: obligation schedule with next due dates
preconditions: At least one dated status observation exists
Obligation definitions carry authority, frequency and consequence
Status mapping tables are versioned and available
effects: Persists a status observation record rather than overwriting prior statuses
Regenerates the obligation schedule as a new version
Emits warnings where a value is older than its source's update cadence

functions.name: Publish governed projection
functions.description: Emit a scoped projection of the organization record — public directory card, compliance profile, lineage view or ownership disclosure — applying disclosure classification, minimisation and licence constraints.
preconditions: The projection is defined in the disclosure and retention policy
Source licences permit redistribution of every included field
Personal-data minimisation rules have been applied
effects: Records a disclosure event with audience, projection, policy version and timestamp
Suppresses fields carrying protection flags or incompatible licences
Attaches attribution and licence notices required by upstream sources

functions.name: Apply retention or erasure action
functions.description: Execute the retention decision for a field group or record: archive, delete, or minimise to a tombstone, with evidence of the action.
preconditions: The retention trigger has occurred and is evidenced
A statutory minimum retention period, where one applies, has elapsed
The authorising agent holds the retention authority for the scope
effects: Removes or archives the in-scope data and writes an irreversible action evidence record
Preserves a tombstone sufficient to keep prior references resolvable
Leaves provenance and audit entries intact unless erasure of those is separately authorised

functions.name: Map record to external standard
functions.description: Produce an aligned representation of the organization record against a named external standard and version, declaring mapping relation types and semantic loss.
preconditions: A versioned mapping table exists for the target standard
The mapping is declared as alignment unless conformance evidence is attached
Elements without a defensible target are marked unmapped rather than forced
effects: Emits the aligned representation with an explicit alignment-not-conformance notice
Records unmapped elements as gaps in the alignment register
Never asserts conformance without attached test or certification evidence

composition.purpose: Internal divisions and departments of the organization are modelled as contained unit instances that resolve back to this organization's canonical key. W3C ORG's OrganizationalUnit exists only within a larger organization and cannot independently hold registry standing, so the split follows a normative distinction rather than convenience.
Operational groupings without external legal identity are contained instances. They inherit organizational context from this model but carry no registration, standing or succession findings.

Alignment target for Organization, FormalOrganization, OrganizationalUnit, OrganizationalCollaboration, Site, Role, Post, Membership and ChangeEvent, and for classification, purpose, identifier, subOrganizationOf, hasSite, hasRegisteredSite, resultedFrom and originalOrganization. Alignment only; no conformance is claimed.

composition.target: ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier and the LEI-CDF reference data model
composition.purpose: Supplies the governed global identifier and the normative separation of entity status from record registration status, validation sources, legal entity events and successor references. Referenced, not embedded, because the Global LEI Index remains the authoritative source.
Provides the typed, period-bounded, quantified control relationship vocabulary and the exception reasons used when a parent cannot be reported.

composition.target: ISO 20275 Entity Legal Forms code list
composition.purpose: Governs the legal form value space, including the reserved codes for forms not yet listed and for entities with no separate legal form. Codes are referenced by list version and are only valid with a jurisdiction.

composition.target: ISO 5009 Official Organizational Roles code list
composition.purpose: Governs the official-role value space for representation, tied to the entity legal form, and provides the normative basis for excluding internal functional titles from statutory representation claims.
Supplies the governed register code space used to qualify every registry entry and validation source across 232 jurisdictions.

composition.target: ISO 3166 country and subdivision codes via the GLEIF accepted legal jurisdictions list
composition.purpose: Constrains jurisdiction values to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 with ISO 3166-2 subdivisions where legal forms exist only sub-nationally.

composition.target: NACE Rev. 2.1 and ISIC Rev. 5 activity classifications
composition.purpose: Provide the versioned activity code spaces and the correspondence tables required for revision migration and cross-scheme comparison.

composition.target: ISO 6523 International Code Designator register (as operated in business networks)
composition.purpose: Defines the scheme-designator plus value pattern used for both qualified identifiers and electronic business addresses, and is the structural basis required for the EU European Unique Identifier.

Ownership and control statements compose with this model: entity records align to the organization record while person records and their privacy obligations are delegated. Interests, share ranges, component records and per-statement source metadata are adopted rather than re-invented.

Publication-side alignment for directory and web projections, confirming the identifier surface and profile fields. It is a projection vocabulary and is never treated as the semantic authority for registration or standing.

Mixed in across all findings to attribute assertions to agents, derive record versions from sources and separate event time from observation time using qualified provenance where circumstances matter.

Registration authorities are themselves organizations with their own governance, coverage and update cadence; this model references their codes and entries without absorbing their institutional model.
Officers, authorised representatives and beneficial owners are person subjects held elsewhere; this model stores only references so that personal-data access and retention rules stay in one place.
Object clauses, powers, decision procedures and amendment rules are referenced from the purpose and representation findings rather than duplicated, keeping a single authoritative text.
Person-to-organization working relations resolve against the identity kept here; membership and role occupancy semantics are delegated to that model.
Presence points reference place records for geometry, building identity and postal normalisation; this model keeps only the presence assertion, its role and its validity.

composition.target: Statistical business register units (legal unit, enterprise, enterprise group, local unit)
composition.purpose: Alignment only: statistical units follow control and economic activity rather than legal personality, so the mapping is recorded as a classification and must never drive merging or splitting of organization records.
Ownership of the record and issuance of access grants over it are governed by the catalogue's service models; this model supplies the disclosure classes and scopes those services enforce.
Every lifecycle event, resolution decision, disclosure and retention action emits an audit facet, satisfying the append-only requirements stated in the artifact rules.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must declare a single owner package for WM-ORG-001 that holds the canonical organization records, the identifier scheme catalogue and the alignment register, and must name a responsible steward reachable through an officer of the organization or its delegate.

The owner package must publish its identifier priority configuration — which master systems are authoritative, which governed global identifiers are accepted, and the UUID or ULID generator used for dimension-assigned keys — so that key selection is reproducible and auditable.

The owner package must pin the versions of every external code list it consumes (entity legal forms, official roles, registration authorities, accepted jurisdictions, activity classifications, identifier scheme designators) and must record the pinned version on every coded value it writes.
The owner package must declare the disclosure and retention policy version in force and the licences under which each ingested source may be redistributed, before any projection is published.
The owner package must expose a conflict register and a named resolution authority for cases where two sources disagree about the same organization fact.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a stable, dereferenceable namespace for organization records under the adopting Dimension, with the model's stable identifiers (bundle, layer, finding, data element, artifact, function ids) as lower-kebab-case path segments beneath it. External code values must always be carried as a scheme-designator plus value pair rather than flattened into a local string, so that a value can never be reinterpreted under the wrong scheme. Do not mint namespace segments from names, addresses or dates; segments derive only from canonical keys. Local extensions live under an explicitly separated extension segment and must never shadow a governed element name.
registry_links: vr.wm-org-001 is the registry entry for this model; nav path NAV.SOC.ORG.ORG, domain tags SOC.ORG.ORG, legacy alias O1.
CONTAINS relations to WM-ORG-002 (organizational units) and WM-ORG-003 (teams) are declared in the catalogue relations file and are instance-level containment, not schema inheritance.

External governed registries referenced by version: entity legal forms, official organizational roles, registration authorities, accepted legal jurisdictions, activity classifications and identifier scheme designators.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form is the semantic record, not any serialization: property order, whitespace, key quoting and file layout carry no meaning and must be normalised away before comparison or digesting.

Coded values canonicalise to the pair (scheme designator with version, value) with the value preserved exactly as issued, including case and check characters; never uppercase, trim or reformat an issued identifier.
All timestamps canonicalise to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; dates that are genuinely date-only remain full-dates and are not promoted to timestamps with a fabricated time.
Names and addresses canonicalise to the source language and script with a language tag; transliterations are additional values with a transliteration flag and never replace the source form.

Absent values canonicalise to explicit absence markers with a reason (not applicable, unknown, suppressed, pending) rather than to null or empty string, because the four cases have different consequences.
patch_rules: Every change is expressed as a patch carrying the target canonical key, the prior version tag, the asserting agent, the source reference and an RFC 3339 observation timestamp; blind overwrites are rejected.
Patches to coded values must state the code-list version under which the new value is valid; a code-list version bump is itself a patch and must be recorded as such.

Corrections and lifecycle changes are distinct patch classes: a correction fixes a previously wrong assertion and preserves the erroneous value in history, while a lifecycle change records a real-world transition with its own effective date.
Patches that would change the canonical key are rejected; key change is performed only by an explicit merge, split or supersession operation that leaves the prior key resolvable as a tombstone.
Patch application is idempotent under the same prior version tag and observation timestamp, so replayed ingestion cannot create duplicate history.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new optional data element, artifact, question or alignment is a minor change; removing or narrowing an element, tightening cardinality, or changing the meaning of a code is a major change requiring a new model version.

Code-list version upgrades are non-breaking only when the correspondence is one-to-one; any one-to-many or many-to-one mapping must be flagged for review and recorded with a mapping ambiguity note rather than applied silently.
Consumers must tolerate unknown additional elements and must not infer meaning from element order or from the presence of an extension segment.
Removing a disclosure class or widening a projection's field set is a breaking change for downstream licence compliance and requires policy re-approval before release.
Deprecated elements remain readable for at least one major version with a deprecation notice and a documented replacement path.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the system of record for the artifact, such as a register code plus entry or filing number, an issuing authority's document reference, or a publisher-assigned statement identifier.

Governed global identifier or IRI: a scheme-qualified identifier from a governed registry, such as an ISO 17442 legal entity identifier, an ISO 6523 scheme designator plus value, or a dereferenceable IRI minted under a governed namespace.

UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above exists; the assignment is recorded with its generator, assigning agent and timestamp so it can be audited and never silently regenerated.
A date, a name, an address, a hash of mutable content or a file path is never an identifier; where such values appear in a key they must be reduced to attributes.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded in RFC 3339 format with seconds and either an explicit numeric UTC offset or Z; date-only facts are recorded as RFC 3339 full-dates and are never padded with a fabricated time. Event time (when a fact became true), authority recording time (when a source registered it) and observation or ingestion time (when this system learned it) are stored as separate fields, and no two may be inferred from one another. Where the source offset is unknown, that is recorded as an explicit precision or offset-unknown marker rather than defaulting to UTC.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts (extracts, observation records, event journal entries, decision logs, assessments, schedules, policy versions, mapping releases) are named by their stable subject key plus a monotonically increasing sequence or a lexicographically sortable ULID, with the RFC 3339 timestamp carried as an attribute and never as the name. Sequences are per subject and per artifact class, are never reused after deletion, and gaps are permitted and must not be interpreted as data loss without an accompanying tombstone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every retained artifact carries a content digest computed over its canonical form, the algorithm identifier, the retrieval or generation timestamp, the asserting agent and the source licence. Artifacts backing legal or registry facts are stored immutably: corrections create a new version linked to the prior one by a derivation edge rather than mutating the original. Journals, decision logs and audit facets are append-only; deletion is permitted only through an authorised retention action that leaves an irreversible action evidence record and a tombstone sufficient to keep prior references resolvable.

policies: External standards are alignments. No conformance to any standard, ontology or code list may be claimed without attached test or certification evidence, and every mapping must declare its relation type and its semantic loss.

Absence is data. Unknown, not-applicable, suppressed and pending are distinct recorded states with reasons and review dates; a field is never left empty to mean any of them, and a missing parent, identifier or address is recorded with an explicit exception reason rather than omitted.
The organization's own existence and the standing of any record about it are separate state machines and must never be collapsed into a single status field.

Personal data reaching this model through officers, representatives and beneficial owners is held by reference and minimised before any projection; personal-data classes carry their own retention periods and are never inherited from the organization record's retention.
Registry-sourced data is redistributed only within the licence under which it was obtained, with required attribution attached to the projection.
Identity is never derived from names, addresses or dates; merges and splits require recorded evidence, a confidence statement, a named deciding agent and a reversible tombstone.
Coded values are meaningless without their code-list version; writing a code without its pinned scheme version is a validation failure, not a warning.
Treat W3C ORG, RegOrg, CBV, ISO 17442, ISO 20275, ISIC and NACE as alignments; do not claim conformance without a recorded evidence artifact.
Public directory projections omit identifier history, non-public contact channels and internal purpose drafts; compliance projections require an admitted requester and an audit record.
Dissolution retires the subject but does not reuse identifiers and does not by itself delete lineage.
Stewards of the record are the organization via officers plus named registrars for their copies; Dimension operators may not silently overwrite master-system legal names or legal identifiers.

read: Reads are scoped by projection: a caller receives the field set defined for its audience under the current disclosure policy, with omitted fields reported as omitted rather than silently dropped.
Every read of a restricted or personal-data-bearing scope emits an access audit entry with caller identity, projection, policy version and RFC 3339 timestamp.
Reads return the record version tag and the corroboration level so callers can reason about staleness and can perform safe conditional writes.
Historical reads are supported as-at a supplied observation time, returning what was known then rather than what is known now.
create: Creating an organization record requires a canonical key selected under the identity priority, the jurisdiction of formation and at least one dated source assertion; a name alone is insufficient.
Creation must check governed registries and the local conflict register for an existing record, and must record an explicit non-match decision when it proceeds anyway.
Creation of relationship, ownership and event records is independent of endpoint creation: a relationship may be created with an explicitly unspecified counterparty and a recorded reason.
Every created record carries provenance at creation: source, source type, asserting agent, licence and retrieval timestamp.
update: Updates are patches against a prior version tag; a mismatch is a conflict, is rejected, and is recorded in the conflict register rather than resolved by last-writer-wins.
Updates must classify themselves as correction or lifecycle change, and lifecycle changes must supply an effective date distinct from the observation timestamp.
Prior values are retained as versioned history; overwriting without history is prohibited for any field backed by a registry or legal fact.
Bulk updates from a source refresh must produce per-field conflict observations where they disagree with more strongly corroborated values, instead of overwriting them.
delete: Hard deletion of organization records is prohibited by default; the normal terminal state is a dissolution or supersession event plus a tombstone that keeps prior references resolvable.
Deletion is permitted only through an authorised retention action bound to a retention policy version, an evidenced trigger and an expired statutory minimum period where one applies.
Erasure of personal-data fields is performed by field-group minimisation rather than record deletion, so that the organization record and its provenance survive.
Every deletion or erasure writes an irreversible action evidence record naming the authorising agent, the scope, the policy version and the RFC 3339 execution timestamp.

roles.name: Organization record steward
responsibilities: Own the canonical organization record on behalf of the organization, acting through its officers or their delegate
Approve merges, splits, supersessions and canonical key changes
Maintain the declared purpose, presence and affiliation assertions and confirm their currency

roles.name: Registry liaison
responsibilities: Maintain register codes, credentials and licences for every source register the Dimension ingests from
Schedule and execute registry extract ingestion and reconcile divergences against held values
Track register coverage, update cadence and outage so staleness thresholds remain realistic

roles.name: Reference data curator
responsibilities: Pin, upgrade and publish versions of every governed code list the model consumes
Maintain correspondence tables for activity, legal form, status and identifier schemes, with ambiguity flags
Review one-to-many mappings before any bulk migration is applied

roles.name: Data quality assessor
responsibilities: Run periodic quality assessments covering corroboration, completeness, staleness and conflicts
Assign remediation owners and due dates and verify closure
Publish the assessment history so quality trends are falsifiable

roles.name: Disclosure and privacy officer
responsibilities: Maintain the disclosure classification, licence constraints and minimisation rules per field group
Approve new projections and audience scopes before release
Handle correction and erasure requests and evidence their outcomes

roles.name: Retention authority
responsibilities: Approve and execute retention, archival and erasure actions against the current policy version
Verify that statutory minimum retention periods have elapsed before any deletion
Ensure tombstones preserve enough to keep prior references resolvable

roles.name: Interoperability maintainer
responsibilities: Maintain the alignment register and its declared mapping relations and semantic losses
Reject or downgrade unevidenced conformance claims
Version and publish outbound projections and their omitted-field rationales

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access is granted per scope to a named agent for a declared purpose and period, under the disclosure class of the requested fields and the licence of their sources. Fields that registers publish freely may be exposed in a public projection; licensed, restricted and personal-data-bearing fields require an explicit grant, and personal-data fields are additionally minimised before release.
exceptions: Publicly disclosed registry facts may be served without an individual grant where the source licence permits redistribution and required attribution is attached.
Protected or suppressed values flagged by an authority's protection regime are withheld even from otherwise authorised callers, and the withholding is reported as an omission with a reason.
Emergency or statutory disclosure to a competent authority may bypass the standard grant path but must be recorded with the legal basis, the requesting authority and the scope released.
The organization's own steward may read the full record about that organization, excluding third-party personal data and licensed source content whose terms forbid onward disclosure.
Ownership and beneficial-ownership statements follow the publishing licence attached to their statement set, which may be narrower than the organization record's default class.
Statutory open-register extracts may be disclosed without a private grant when the source register is public.
A successor or acquiring organization may read lineage of a ceased predecessor needed to complete the corporate action.
Non-public contact channels are visible only to organization-steward and agents with a legal-notices exception.
Quality-exception payloads (failed corroboration) are visible to compliance-reader even when full presence detail is not.
audit_requirements: Every read of a restricted, licensed or personal-data-bearing scope is logged with caller identity, scope, projection, policy version and RFC 3339 timestamp.
Every grant issuance, modification and revocation is logged with the authorising agent, purpose, scope and validity period.
Every merge, split, correction, deletion and erasure writes an append-only entry that cannot be edited, only superseded.
Audit entries are retained at least as long as the data they describe, and their own deletion requires separate authorisation recorded outside the deleted scope.
Access logs are themselves classified as personal-data-bearing where they identify natural persons and are minimised accordingly.
Every compliance-profile read records requester, purpose, projection and datetime.
Every create or update of legal name, legal identifier, legal form, status or successor links records actor, evidence reference, effective time and recorded time.
Identifier resolution that returns DUPLICATE, ANNULLED or successor-required must be auditable.

read_order: AGENTS.md first, to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before touching any data — this holds even when the storage is MongoDB or the interface is MCP, because the bootstrap contract is storage- and interface-neutral.
Specification URL next, to load the model semantics: scope, boundaries, bundles, layers, findings, data elements and artifact rules.
Storage type URL, to learn how the semantic record is projected into the concrete store, including canonicalization, versioning and digest conventions.
Interface URL, to learn the available operations, projections, scopes and error semantics before attempting any read or write.
Processes URL, to learn the governed procedures for ingestion, resolution, lifecycle assertion, quality assessment, disclosure and retention.
Pinned code list versions and the disclosure and retention policy version, before writing any coded value or publishing any projection.

coverage.claim: The synthesized WM-ORG-001 covers the organization as an externally addressable subject: designation and name history, scheme-qualified identity and canonical key selection, legal form and entity category, formality spectrum and home legal jurisdiction, activity and statistical classification, declared purpose and scale, formation, registry entry, standing and recurring obligations, lifecycle events, succession, dissolution, organization-side control and ownership endpoints, official roles and affiliation, presence and reachability, and record provenance, stewardship, quality, disclosure, retention and interoperability. Coverage is strongest for registered legal entities in jurisdictions carried by the GLEIF registration-authority and ELF lists and for European classification schemes; it is demonstrably weaker for informal, customary, religious and indigenous collectives, for North American activity classification, and for redomiciliation and post-strike-off restoration. No claim of universal or metaphysical completeness is made.

checklist.notes: Scheme-qualified identifiers, canonical key priority (master-system, governed global/IRI, dimension-assigned UUID/ULID), alias retention, name forms and entity resolution with recorded evidence and confidence. Grounded in LEI-CDF, the ISO 6523 ICD register, BODS identifiers and the EU requirement that the EUID be ISO 6523 compliant.

Formation act and creation date, entity status separated from record registration status with real enumerations, qualified status detail, recurring obligations with due dates and lapse consequences, lifecycle event journal and succession/continuity decisions. Grounded in LEI-CDF LegalEntityEvents, Companies House status enumerations and W3C ORG ChangeEvent.

Consolidation, branch and fund links with typed periods, quantifiers and eight exception reasons; ownership and beneficial-ownership interests with direct/indirect, share ranges and component records for indirect chains; official roles and non-controlling affiliations kept separate. Grounded in RR-CDF, BODS and ISO 5009.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z; event time, authority recording time and observation/ingestion time held separately and never inferred from one another; validity intervals on names, forms, appointments, sites and interests; three distinct relationship period types; as-at historical reads.

Per-assertion source, source type, licence, retrieval timestamp and asserting agent; derivation typed as copy, revision, transformation or inference; a provenance graph artifact using PROV-O starting-point and qualified terms with prov:Organization as agent.

Two senses are distinguished and both covered: ownership of the organization (interests, beneficial ownership, consolidation, global decision centre) and ownership of the record (steward role, asserting agent, publisher, licence).

Graded corroboration (pending, entity-supplied-only, partially corroborated, fully corroborated) against a named validation authority with validation documents; identifier syntax and check-character rules; version-tag concurrency; partial-data markers; explicit non-match records.

Deny-by-default with grants scoped to bundle, layer, finding and artifact; five named exception classes including authority-suppressed values and statutory disclosure; audit requirements on reads, grants and mutations; projections report omitted fields rather than dropping them silently.

Per-disclosure-class retention with evidenced triggers, statutory minimum checks, field-group minimisation for personal data instead of record deletion, tombstones that keep prior references resolvable, and irreversible action evidence records. Hard deletion of organization records is prohibited by default.

Alignment-not-conformance policy, versioned mapping tables with relation types and declared semantic loss, activity-scheme correspondence tables with mapping cardinality, status-value mapping with loss notes, and a conflict register with per-consumer precedence rules.

Legal form (ISO 20275 with reserved 8888/9999), entity category and subcategory, legal personality, activity codes under versioned schemes, statistical unit alignment, size class and non-profit status.

Jurisdiction constrained to ISO 3166-1/-2 via the accepted jurisdictions list, registered versus operating locations, branches, served areas and delegation of geometry to the place model. Address language and script are treated as first-class.

Registration authorities from a governed 232-jurisdiction list, validation authority, official organizational roles tied to legal form with representation powers and joint-signature rules, granting authorities for non-profit status, and statutory or treaty formation for public bodies.

Personal data held by reference only, disclosure classes per field group, minimisation before projection, authority protection and suppression flags, and correction/erasure request handling with evidenced outcomes.

Absence is modelled as data with reasons and review dates: reserved legal-form codes, reporting exception reasons for unreportable parents, unspecified-entity reasons in ownership, unknown-date markers, registration-not-applicable for informal organizations.
Size and relationship quantifiers carry method, unit, reference period and producing party, with consolidation scope declared; match confidence is expressed on a named scale.

Transport security, authentication mechanisms, key management and integrity signing beyond content digests are deliberately not modelled here. They belong to the storage and interface projections and to platform service models; no cited primary source in this set governs them at the semantic layer, so asserting structure would be unsupported.

Eleven governed functions with preconditions and effects cover resolution, ingestion, event assertion, continuity evaluation, deduplication, classification migration, relationship recording, standing evaluation, projection publication, retention action and standard mapping.

known_omissions: Informal, customary, religious and indigenous organizations are structurally accommodated (registration is optional, identity can rest on a dimension-assigned key) but are not positively grounded: none of the cited primary sources model them, so the treatment is a designed accommodation rather than an evidenced structure.

Financial standing, credit, sanctions and watchlist status are omitted. They are consumer-specific assessments over this record, change on a different cadence, and would import licensing and accuracy obligations that do not belong to organizational identity.
Trademark and trade-name rights over organization names are omitted; the naming layer records name forms and validity but makes no claim about who is entitled to use a name.

Internal governance procedure — board composition rules, quorum, voting and delegation mechanics — is referenced to the charter model and not modelled here, so questions about how a decision was validly taken cannot be answered from this model alone.

Digital-identity credentials for organizations (verifiable credentials, organizational wallets, vLEI-style role credentials) are not modelled. They were not verifiable from the primary sources retrieved in this pass and would need their own evidenced layer.

Multi-jurisdiction tax identity (VAT group membership, permanent establishment, tax residence) is only touched through identifier schemes; its substantive rules are jurisdiction-specific and belong to a tax model.
Organization-to-organization contractual relationships (joint ventures beyond W3C ORG's OrganizationalCollaboration, consortia, franchise networks) are only weakly covered by the affiliation finding.
Historical and defunct organizations predating modern registers are accommodated by unknown-date markers but have no evidenced identity strategy in the cited sources.
Cross-border redomiciliation/continuation as a standardized event type.
Restoration after administrative strike-off as a global code.
Name reservation and companies in formation before legal personality.
Series LLCs, protected-cell companies and similar internal liability partitions.
DAOs and smart-contract collectives without a register or LEI-eligible contract capacity.
Indigenous nations and polities as sovereigns rather than organizations.
A single global nonprofit/charity classification.
Sanctions, licensing and fitness-to-operate registers.
GLEIF RR-CDF Level 2 parent, fund-relationship and reporting-exception records.
Officer/director registers as a governance model (ISO 5009 roles discovered but not fetched as a governing source).
NAICS as a first-party Bureau source was not fetched; North American activity is a likely regional omission.
Core Public Organisation Vocabulary is a specialized public-body profile not fully expanded here.
conflicts: Directive (EU) 2017/1132 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/1042 could not be rendered in full by the retrieval tool; the EUID provisions cited in SRC-016 were surfaced from EUR-Lex indexed text rather than a full-text read, and must be verified against the Official Journal before being relied on normatively. This is the weakest evidential link in the model and the EUID-specific data element should be treated as provisional.

FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 on basic company information and beneficial ownership were unreachable (HTTP 403) in this pass. The beneficial-ownership structure therefore rests on BODS, an authority-tier-2 standard, rather than on the intergovernmental requirement it implements; the ownership layer should be re-grounded when FATF text is retrievable.

Status vocabularies conflict irreconcilably across sources: LEI-CDF uses a two-value entity status plus a ten-value registration status, while Companies House uses a twelve-value national enumeration mixing legal states (dissolved, liquidation) with record states (removed, open). Any normalised status is lossy, which is why the model requires both the source value and the mapping loss note to be retained.

'Organization' scope conflicts between sources: W3C ORG admits informal collectives, LEI-CDF is restricted to entities that can be validated against a registration authority, and BODS distinguishes registeredEntity from legalEntity, arrangement, anonymousEntity and unknownEntity. This model takes the broad W3C reading and treats registry-backed structure as conditional.

Legal form and activity classification are jurisdiction-bound and revision-bound: the same organization can hold non-equivalent NACE and ISIC codes, and a legal form may exist only at ISO 3166-2 subdivision level. Cross-scheme comparison without a declared correspondence table and mapping cardinality is unsound.

Statistical enterprise boundaries follow control while legal-unit boundaries follow legal personality, so official statistics and legal registers will legitimately disagree about how many organizations exist in a group. The model records this as alignment and forbids using statistical units to merge or split records.
W3C ORG recommends one legally recognized skos:prefLabel; RegOrg and CBV allow multiple legalName values in multilingual jurisdictions; LEI-CDF allows one Primary LegalName plus OtherEntityNames.
ORG identifier is a typed literal; RegOrg/CBV require a structured ADMS Identifier; both can be derived in one direction only.
LEI EntityStatus, LEI RegistrationStatus and national orgStatus vocabularies are three different state machines often wrongly merged.
NACE Rev. 2, NACE Rev. 2.1, ISIC Rev. 4 and ISIC Rev. 5 are related but not interchangeable; schema.org still cites ISIC Rev. 4.
ELF codes are unique per jurisdiction-form pair; similarly named forms (SA, LLC, GmbH) are not equivalent across borders.
AssociatedEntity is deprecated in LEI-CDF 3.1 in favour of events and relationship records.
A GLEIF BRANCH category is not an org:OrganizationalUnit and not necessarily an org:Site.
CBV/RegOrg exclude informal organizations that W3C ORG and this catalogue purpose explicitly include.
regional_assumptions: The registration and standing bundle is strongest for jurisdictions covered by the GLEIF registration-authority list (232 jurisdictions, 1,050+ registers); coverage depth, update cadence and data quality vary sharply between them and are not uniform.

Activity classification assumes access to NACE Rev. 2.1 (European statistics from 2025) or ISIC Rev. 5 (endorsed 2023); jurisdictions on older revisions or on wholly national schemes require correspondence tables that may be one-to-many.

The EUID and BRIS interconnection provisions apply only to EU member-state registers and to companies and branches within their scope; they are not a global identifier mechanism and must not be assumed elsewhere.

Electronic addressing examples derive from a European business network; the scheme-designator plus value pattern generalises, but the specific designators and the availability of a participant registry do not.

The personal-data treatment assumes a jurisdiction with data-protection obligations over officer and beneficial-owner data and with a correction/erasure route; jurisdictions with full public disclosure of officer data, or with none, will need different disclosure classes.
Non-profit and public-benefit status is granted per jurisdiction under non-comparable criteria; the status code is only interpretable together with its granting jurisdiction and instrument.
Latin-script assumptions are avoided in the model but persist in several cited code lists, which supply transliterations rather than treating non-Latin forms as primary.
Home legal jurisdiction can be expressed as ISO 3166-1 or 3166-2.
Where a business register exists, it is the master for legal name, legal identifier and national legal form.
EU interoperability prefers NACE; global statistical comparison prefers ISIC; other regions use national schemes mapped to ISIC.
LEI is widely available for contract-capable entities but is not mandatory for all organization types or informal collectives.
ELF list v1.6 still uses reserved 8888/9999 where research is incomplete, including some legal forms not yet enumerated.
French overseas territories sharing French legislation inherit French ELF codes and legal jurisdiction France, per GLEIF ELF notes.
Public access to company extracts varies; UK/EU open-register practice must not be assumed for all states.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample — organization without any register: community groups, unincorporated associations and informal collectives have no registry entry, no legal form code and no scheme identifier. The model survives because registration, legal form and standing are optional, identity may rest on a dimension-assigned UUID/ULID, and the entity-category finding forces the applicability question explicitly. A structure that required a registration number would have been rejected.

Counterexample — branch with its own identifier but no legal personality: a branch can hold an LEI under EntityCategory BRANCH while being legally part of another entity. This breaks any rule equating 'has a global identifier' with 'is a legal person', so legal personality is modelled as a separate flag and the branch link is a typed relationship rather than internal containment.

Counterexample — one organization, many contradictory registers: a multinational may be simultaneously ACTIVE in a global index and 'liquidation' in a national register, with different legal names in each. Rather than picking a winner, the model requires the conflict to be recorded with both sources and resolved per consumer through a precedence rule, and forbids overwriting a more strongly corroborated value during bulk refresh.

Rejected structure — a single 'status' field: attractive and near-universal in practice, but LEI-CDF's separation of entity status from registration status plus Companies House's mixed enumeration prove that at least two independent state machines exist. A single field was rejected as unsupported and actively lossy.

Rejected structure — 'organization = legal unit': Eurostat register practice shows an enterprise may span several legal units and that group boundaries follow control. Equating the organization with the legal unit would have made statistical alignment impossible, so statistical unit type became a classification with an explicit prohibition on using it to merge or split records.

Rejected structure — name-based or address-based identity: names are non-unique within and across registers, change without identity change, and exist in multiple scripts; addresses are shared by thousands of service-provided entities. Both were excluded from every identity strategy, and the artifact rules state this explicitly.

Rejected structure — folding beneficial ownership persons into this model: it would import personal-data retention, minimisation and access obligations onto the organization record. BODS's separation of entity, person and relationship records supports delegating person records, so only organization-side endpoints are kept.

Stress test — silent absence: a naive model represents a missing parent, an unlisted legal form and a suppressed address all as null. The cited sources supply four distinct mechanisms (eight reporting exception reasons, reserved codes 8888/9999, unspecified-entity reasons, authority suppression flags), so explicit absence-with-reason was made a policy rather than a convention.

Stress test — conformance inflation: it would be easy to claim conformance to W3C ORG, ISO 17442 and schema.org simultaneously. No test or certification evidence was retrieved for any of them, so all are recorded as ALIGN or REFERENCE, and the mapping function is required to attach an alignment-not-conformance notice.
Informal community versus registered company: refusing a fake company number while still assigning a Dimension id and names.
Lapsed LEI versus dissolved entity: a non-renewed identifier must not be treated as cessation.
Duplicate LEI exclusivity violation: DUPLICATE status marks the non-surviving identifier, not a second organization.
International branch with own LEI versus a mere site of headquarters.
Merger where the surviving legal entity keeps its id versus a new entity that must receive a new canonical id.
Two official legal names in a bilingual jurisdiction versus a translation stored as a trading name.
Subsidiary that is a full Organization versus a department modelled as WM-ORG-002.
Government ministry that can contract without incorporation, eligible for LEI as RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY.
Sole proprietor where the human person is a sibling and only the business capacity is this subject.
Activity code copied from an old NACE Rev. 2 filing after the statistical program moved to Rev. 2.1 without correspondence.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently returned entry_kind 'entity' and the subject behaves as one: a persistent, externally addressable subject bearing identity, classification, standing and a lifecycle, not an event, relation or service. The one live boundary divergence is control and ownership: the base retains organization-side endpoints of consolidation, group and beneficial-ownership relationship records while Grok delegates them entirely to a sibling. Adjudicated in favour of the base, because BODS itself separates entity records, person records and relationship records, so keeping only the entity-side endpoint is evidenced rather than invented, and the base already delegates person records with their distinct privacy, access and retention obligations. The ownership layer is nonetheless marked as the seam to re-test when the sibling relationship model is registered, so this acceptance is of the base's endpoint-only reading, not of a full relationship model living inside WM-ORG-001.

decisions.rationale: Nine evidenced neighbor notes, each carrying an operational discrimination test for the hard cases (branch holding its own LEI, statistical enterprise spanning legal units, sole proprietor, register-as-institution, fund and sub-fund, informal collectives, BODS person records, site and place), plus explicit prohibition rules. Grok's boundary is cleaner only where it delegates ownership wholesale, and it leaves umbrella, branch and successor relations half-inside. Size was not the deciding factor.

decisions.concept: Control and ownership inside the organization model
decisions.disposition: Base reading retained; endpoint-only scope confirmed
decisions.rationale: Grok places beneficial ownership, shareholding and GLEIF Level 2 records entirely out of scope. The base keeps only the organization-side endpoints, which BODS supports by separating entity, person and relationship records. Retaining the endpoint preserves group and consolidation answerability without importing person-level privacy, access and retention obligations.

decisions.concept: Home legal jurisdiction as a first-class finding
decisions.rationale: The base makes legal form jurisdiction-dependent and cites the accepted-jurisdictions code list, yet never establishes the jurisdiction of formation as its own fact, leaving a dangling dependency and no answer for multi-register countries.

The base declares a broad W3C ORG reading that admits informal collectives but implements it only as an exception question under a GLEIF category vocabulary. The W3C ORG, RegOrg and CBV three-step spectrum gives that reading real structure.

decisions.concept: National legal form vocabulary alongside ELF
decisions.rationale: ELF is a cross-border alignment and does not replace the home register's own form code when that register is master; the cross-border false-equivalence guard for SA, LLC and GmbH is absent from the base.

decisions.concept: Dissolution as a terminal state distinct from succession
decisions.rationale: The base models termination only as a transition to a successor and cannot represent cessation without one, winding-up in progress, or the rule that identifiers remain historical keys and are never reassigned.
The base's checklist claims steward coverage that no finding implements; per-field-group master assignment and authorised change agents are distinct from provenance attribution.

decisions.concept: LEI and global identifier scheme specifics (grok lei-and-global-schemes)
decisions.rationale: The ISO 17442 eligibility test and LEI exclusivity rule are genuinely unanswerable from the base's generic scheme-qualified identifier finding, but Grok's evidence is an ISO catalogue landing page, not the normative text, and a scheme-specific finding would cut against the base's deliberate format-neutral generalisation. Re-open once ISO 17442-1:2020 normative text is readable.

The base's entity-status-vs-registration-status finding already asks for qualifying status detail and the governing procedure for administration, liquidation and struck-off-pending, and already requires the source value plus a mapping loss note. Only the restoration and redomiciliation gap is genuinely new, and both providers agree no primary cross-jurisdictional schema exists for it, so it moves to deferred research rather than into structure.

The base's activity-code-assignments finding already asks which activity is principal and by what criterion principality was determined, and separately asks whether the code was assigned by the organization, a register or a statistical authority.

The base's electronic-addresses-and-channels finding already covers channel purpose including legal service, per-channel verification, and retirement with redirect or tombstone, on a stronger scheme-qualified footing than the schema.org-backed alternative.

decisions.disposition: Rejected as weakly supported and overlapping
decisions.rationale: Charity and nonprofit status is already carried by the base's purpose-and-nonprofit-status finding with a granting authority and instrument. The remaining taxonomic-scheme content rests on W3C ORG plus a tier-3 schema.org reference, and Grok itself records the absence of any cross-border nonprofit classification as a gap.

decisions.concept: Multiple co-equal legal names in multilingual jurisdictions
decisions.disposition: Accepted as a required correction to the base naming finding, not as a new finding
decisions.rationale: RegOrg and SEMIC CBV make legalName a repeatable language-tagged literal precisely because bilingual jurisdictions grant several legal names of equal standing, which contradicts the base question asking which single name form is the legal name. Adding Grok's finding would duplicate name-forms-and-validity, so this is recorded as a framing correction and carried as a publication hold instead.

decisions.disposition: Accepted as a constraint on the base naming layer, not as a new finding
decisions.rationale: RegOrg and CBV forbid storing a translation of the legal name in an alternative or trading name field. The base already separates name kinds and language tags but states no such prohibition, and a prohibition is a rule on an existing finding rather than a finding of its own.

resolve-identifier, record-legal-entity-event and validate-current-standing map one-to-one onto the base's resolve-organization-identifier, assert-lifecycle-event and evaluate-record-standing; syndicate-directory-card and disclose-registry-extract are scoped emissions already covered by publish-projection; construct-succession-lineage is the read side of evaluate-succession-continuity and the lineage view publish-projection already names. No function addition would add capability.

decisions.disposition: Retained from base; no Grok equivalent
decisions.rationale: Grok has no counterpart to the Eurostat business-register distinction between legal unit, enterprise and enterprise group, nor to the prohibition on using statistical units to merge or split organization records. This is a base-only strength that the synthesis must preserve intact.

The base records schema.org as a primary source at authority tier 2 while Grok records it as non-primary at tier 3. Grok's classification is the defensible one for a community vocabulary used as a discovery mapping, and both models already treat it as alignment rather than conformance.

The base marks transport security, authentication, key management and integrity signing as deliberately unmodelled because no cited primary source governs them at the semantic layer. Grok asserts no structure there either, so the honest declared gap is carried forward rather than papered over.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete and must be run before publication: every accepted source URL must be re-fetched and its version pin confirmed. The two providers cite different GLEIF URL paths for the same two documents (LEI-CDF 3.1 under /common-data-file-format/current-versions/ versus /common-data-file-format/, and the ELF list under /code-lists/ versus the bare path), so at least one variant in each pair is stale or a redirect and the canonical form must be established.

Multi-profile domain validation has not been performed. The structure must be exercised against at least six distinct profiles before publication: a registered company with an LEI, an unregistered informal collective with no scheme identifier, an international branch holding its own LEI without separate legal personality, a fund with an umbrella and management relationship, a resident government entity formed by statute, and a sole proprietor whose legal person is a natural person. Coverage claims are provisional until each profile is walked end to end.

The EUID and BRIS provisions carried by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/1042 were surfaced from indexed EUR-Lex text rather than a full-text read, by the base provider's own admission. The EUID-specific data element must be treated as provisional and verified against the Official Journal before any normative reliance.

FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 were unreachable (HTTP 403), so the beneficial-ownership structure rests on BODS at authority tier 2 rather than on the intergovernmental requirement it implements. The ownership layer must be re-grounded before it is published as an authority-backed structure.

The base naming finding asks which single name form is the legal name, which is wrong for multilingual jurisdictions where RegOrg and SEMIC CBV make legalName a repeatable language-tagged literal with several co-equal legal names. The naming layer must be reframed to admit multiple co-equal legal names, with the RegOrg prohibition on storing translations in alternative-name fields, before that layer is published as normative.

ISO 17442-1:2020 and ISO 20275 were cited from standards-catalogue landing pages, not normative text. Any statement in the synthesized model that reads as a conformance or eligibility rule derived from those standards must be marked alignment-only until the normative text is obtained.

ISO 5009 is carried by the base as a tier-1 primary source for official organizational roles while the other provider records it as discovered but not fetched. The official-roles finding's specific claims (role counts, jurisdiction coverage, tie to ELF, exclusion of internal functional titles) must be confirmed against the fetched code list before publication.
deferredResearch: ISO 17442-1:2020 normative text, to ground LEI eligibility (whether the subject can enter contracts or is legally or financially responsible) and LEI exclusivity and non-reassignment as evidenced constraints.
